- speckit-analyze: Perform a non-destructive cross-artifact consistency and quality analysis across spec.md, plan.md, and tasks.md after task generation.
- speckit-checklist: Generate a custom checklist for the current feature based on user requirements.
- speckit-clarify: Identify underspecified areas in the current feature spec by asking up to 5 highly targeted clarification questions and encoding answers back into the spec.
- speckit-constitution: Create or update the project constitution from interactive or provided principle inputs, ensuring all dependent templates stay in sync.
- speckit-implement: Execute the implementation plan by processing and executing all tasks defined in tasks.md
- speckit-plan: Execute the implementation planning workflow using the plan template to generate design artifacts.
- speckit-specify: Create or update the feature specification from a natural language feature description.
- speckit-tasks: Generate an actionable, dependency-ordered tasks.md for the feature based on available design artifacts.
- speckit-taskstoissues: Convert existing tasks into actionable, dependency-ordered GitHub issues for the feature based on available design artifacts.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codex:rescue: Delegate investigation, an explicit fix request, or follow-up rescue work to the Codex rescue subagent
- codex:setup: Check whether the local Codex CLI is ready and optionally toggle the stop-time review gate
- codex:codex-cli-runtime: Internal helper contract for calling the codex-companion runtime from Claude Code
- codex:codex-result-handling: Internal guidance for presenting Codex helper output back to the user
- codex:gpt-5-4-prompting: Internal guidance for composing Codex and GPT-5.4 prompts for coding, review, diagnosis, and research tasks inside the Codex Claude Code plugin
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

2	
3	**Branch**: `364-devcontainer-refactor` | **Date**: 2026-06-03 (revised after E-1/E-2 resolutions) | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

See scoreboard below. Decisions and contracts are not blocked by the deferrals. Ready for `/speckit-tasks`; all three deferrals become first tasks (T022, T006, T005 respectively).
6	
7	## Summary
8	
9	Refactor `.devcontainer/` so that the official `ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node` Feature installs Node 22 (with two-layer pinning: digest-pinned Feature reference plus `version: "22"` option), while repo-coupled, gate-critical, and determinism-sensitive tools (gitleaks SHA-verified, Playwright apt deps, unzip, uv, Spec Kit, **`gh`**, **and `entire`**) stay in the Dockerfile. `gh` installs via the official `cli.github.com` apt repository with signed keyring, ARG-pinned `GH_VERSION`, `apt-mark hold`, and `gh --version` validation. `entire` (git observability layer for AI agent sessions, ALREADY wired into this repo's `.husky/` scripts and `.entire/settings.json`) installs via the official `entire.io` install script with `ENTIRE_VERSION` ARG pin and the pair `entire enable --agent claude-code && entire agent add codex` in postCreateCommand (FR-020; revised from the earlier-prescribed but invalid `entire enable --yes --agent claude-code,codex` once `--agent` was confirmed single-value in entire CLI v0.7.3) — the husky `.husky/_/commit-msg` dispatcher-overwrite this performs is the accepted constitutional asymmetry per `LOCAL_CI_PARITY_INVARIANTS.md` row 7f, requiring no constitution amendment. Default `gh` and `entire` authentication each uses a one-time interactive `<tool> login` persisted via its own named Docker volume (`ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config` and `ado-git-repo-insights-entire-config`). Personal AI **client** tooling (Claude Code, Codex) stays out of the tracked image per FR-008; entire (observability infrastructure, not an AI client) is carved out via FR-008 and installed per FR-020. SSH/GPG forwarding and `containerEnv` PAT injection remain enterprise-override-only. The refactor preserves the constitution's local/CI parity invariants (QG-35..QG-56) and limits CI changes to the `publish-devcontainer` job's existing surface unless a post-build smoke step turns out to be necessary (FR-019).
10	
11	## Technical Context
12	
13	**Language/Version**: Dockerfile (BuildKit-compatible), `devcontainer.json` (Dev Containers spec), bash for scripts, Python 3.12 for verification helpers.
14	**Primary Dependencies**: `ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node` (digest-pinned, `version: "22"`); `cli.github.com` apt repo (signed keyring, `GH_VERSION=2.93.0`); upstream `github.com/github/spec-kit` at commit `c3194c543b53c67e85d996fe90bc1b26813b0e3b` (tag `v0.9.2`); **`entire.io` install script (`ENTIRE_VERSION=0.7.3` per FR-020; SHA-verified release-binary fallback if install script doesn't honor pinning)**; existing pinned versions for uv (0.11.9), gitleaks (8.18.4 SHA-verified), Playwright apt deps (anchored to `extension/package.json::@playwright/test=1.60.0`), pnpm 9.15.0 (via Corepack in Dockerfile — D-1a confirmed the Node Feature's `pnpmVersion` proposals don't include 9.15.0, so pnpm stays in Dockerfile per Version Inventory's fallback path).
15	**Storage**: Named Docker volume `ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config` mounted at `/home/vscode/.config/gh` for `gh` auth state persistence (FR-005). No domain data storage involved.
16	**Testing**: Image-property verification via FR-013 gate (each tool's pinned-version check, `gitleaks detect --config=.gitleaks.toml`, `python scripts/run_pr_preflight.py` exit 0 without `--allow-local-degraded`; `gh auth status` "not logged in" is the documented baseline, NOT a failure). Host-auth verification via FR-014 (two separate success checks for two separate auth surfaces: git HTTPS via credential-helper proxy, `gh` via named-volume persistence). Both gates produce attached verification logs (SC-005, SC-007).
17	**Target Platform**: `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` Dev Container manifests published by the existing `publish-devcontainer` CI job. Host runtimes: macOS (Apple Silicon, native arm64 pull), Linux (native amd64), Windows (via WSL2 or Hyper-V Docker Desktop).
18	**Project Type**: Infrastructure / developer environment. No `src/` tree changes proposed.
19	**Performance Goals**: SC-003 — image size within ±10% of D-4 baseline per architecture (arm64 baseline at spec time: 833,692,081 bytes / ~795 MB at digest `sha256:4af3c965…d93d`; amd64 baseline measured by implementer during controlled D-4 reopen). SC-004 — container-ready wall-clock time within ±20% of D-4 baseline (must be captured on a controlled `Reopen in Container`; cannot be measured retroactively).
20	**Constraints**: Constitution v1.5.0 (QG-35 through QG-56 parity invariants) must hold. No `--no-verify` bypass. Cross-platform Windows/macOS/Linux invariant (QG-39). `gitleaks` parity (QG-56) preserved by keeping the SHA-verified Dockerfile install. `.gitignore` exclusions for `.codex`, `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md` MUST remain intact. **`containerEnv` PAT injection** would be XIX-adjacent (FR-007) and is explicitly NOT the default.
21	**Scale/Scope**: ~6 file changes (`.devcontainer/Dockerfile`, `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, `.devcontainer/README.md`, `.specify/init-options.json` co-commit, `specs/364-devcontainer-refactor/contracts/devcontainer.contract.md` reference). One PR. No source-tree changes.
22	
23	## Constitution Check
24	
25	Gate-by-gate evaluation against [`/.specify/memory/constitution.md`](../../.specify/memory/constitution.md) v1.5.0:
26	
27	| Principle / Gate | Impact | Notes |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| I–XVI (CSV / persistence / identity / runtime / PAT) | None | Refactor does not touch CSV contract, persistence layer, identity keys, or PAT handling. |
30	| XVII (Cross-Agent Compatibility) | Preserved | Refactor is dev-environment scope; pipeline-task code unchanged. |
31	| XIX (PAT Secrecy) | Preserved | Default `gh` auth is named-volume-persisted `gh auth login` (FR-005). PAT injection via `containerEnv` is XIX-adjacent and explicitly reserved as an enterprise override requiring stakeholder approval (FR-007); not the default. No PAT enters image layers, repo files, or process env by default. |
32	| XXVI (Collection-Stable Tests) | None | No test changes proposed. |
33	| QG-35 / QG-36 (parity) | Preserved | No new CI checks at default; `python scripts/run_pr_preflight.py` remains the authoritative local gate (FR-011, FR-013). |
34	| QG-37 (new CI check requires local + doc) | Preserved | Refactor consumes `publish-devcontainer` unchanged unless D-1/D-4 surfaces a digest/verification-output gap (FR-019). Any added CI step under that exception has a local equivalent (FR-013/FR-014). |
35	| QG-38 (`--no-verify` forbidden) | Preserved | Refactor adds no hook-bypass paths. |
36	| QG-39 (cross-platform) | Preserved | Multi-arch image (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64) continues; FR-009 enforces; D-1b checks per-arch availability of the chosen `GH_VERSION`. |
37	| QG-40 (no `typing.Any`) | N/A | No Python code changes in refactor scope. |
38	| QG-41 (zero inline suppressions) | Preserved | Refactor adds no `# noqa` / `# type: ignore` / `// eslint-disable` / `// @ts-ignore`. |
39	| QG-42 (enterprise test coverage) | N/A in source-tree sense; FR-013/FR-014 verification gates cover the refactor's deliverables with attached logs (SC-005, SC-007). |
40	| QG-43..QG-46 (test-floor discipline) | None | No tests added or removed; floor unaffected. |

43	| QG-53..QG-55 (build architecture) | None | Refactor doesn't touch extension tsconfig or Prettier wiring. |
44	| QG-56 (gitleaks parity) | **Preserved** | The Dockerfile's SHA-verified gitleaks install is explicitly kept (FR-004, Version Inventory). No Feature substitution. |
45	| VR-28 / VR-29 / VR-30 (preflight, ratchet-bump) | Preserved | FR-011 requires `python scripts/run_pr_preflight.py` to exit 0 inside the rebuilt container without `--allow-local-degraded`. |
46	
47	**Verdict:** No constitutional violations. The XIX-adjacent path (option (d) of E-2: `containerEnv` PAT injection) is explicitly NOT the default and is governed by FR-007 enterprise-override rules. Adoption of that override in any tracked configuration requires stakeholder approval per the constitutional process — which is exactly what FR-007 documents.

Host-auth verification via FR-014 (two separate success checks for two separate auth surfaces: git HTTPS via credential-helper proxy, `gh` via named-volume persistence). **Target Platform**: `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` Dev Container manifests published by the existing `publish-devcontainer` CI job. Host runtimes: macOS (Apple Silicon, native arm64 pull), Linux (native amd64), Windows (via WSL2 or Hyper-V Docker Desktop).

**Performance Goals**: SC-003 — image size within ±10% of D-4 baseline per architecture (arm64 baseline at spec time: 833,692,081 bytes / ~795 MB at digest `sha256:4af3c965…d93d`; amd64 baseline measured by implementer during controlled D-4 reopen). 147	!f() { /home/vscode/.vscode-server/bin/6a44c352bd24569c417e530095901b649960f9f8/node /tmp/vscode-remote-containers-49fa5eb7-8573-42da-8811-f6395a2e05cb.js git-credential-helper $*; }; f

# Research: Dev Container Refactor (Pre-Planning Discovery Evidence + Resolutions)

**Branch**: `364-devcontainer-refactor`
**Date**: 2026-06-03
**Status**: Discovery substantially complete. **6 of 8 sub-checkpoints executed with real evidence; 2 genuinely deferred to implementer/contributor action** (D-4b container-ready time requires a controlled VS Code `Reopen in Container` event that cannot be triggered from a headless workflow; D-2 Step 3 interactive `gh auth login` is the contributor's first-run action by design — the persistence mechanism it relies on has been independently proven by sentinel-file substitute, see §D-2). All resolutions for E-1, E-2, and the supporting decisions are incorporated; spec is amended; planning proceeds to `/speckit-tasks` with the two named deferrals listed as first tasks.

This document captures the evidence produced by Pre-Planning Discovery checkpoints D-1 through D-4 defined in `spec.md`, and the spec author's decisions that resolve the escalations the evidence surfaced.

---

## Resolutions (executive summary)

| ID | Original status | Resolution | Spec impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **E-1 (premise)** | Wrong | Dev Container Feature `proposals` arrays are UI autocomplete hints, NOT enums. `type: "string"` options accept arbitrary values; the `github-cli` Feature's install script processes non-"latest"/"none" values via `find_version_from_git_tags`. Original "Feature cannot pin" framing was incorrect. | Spec author chose Dockerfile/apt for `gh` anyway (E-1 decision below). Corrected understanding is documented in the spec's D-1 historical note. |
| **E-1 (decision)** | Material | **Install `gh` via `cli.github.com` apt repository in the Dockerfile**, with signed keyring, ARG-pinned `GH_VERSION`, `apt-mark hold gh`, and `gh --version` validation. Multi-arch verification (`amd64` + `arm64`) via D-1b. SHA-verified release-binary path reserved as fallback only if apt cannot satisfy multi-arch. | FR-001 rewritten; FR-003 narrowed (Node-only Feature); FR-004 expanded (gh in Dockerfile-owned inventory); Version Inventory `gh` row rewritten. |
| **E-2 (premise)** | Wrong (in original spec) | VS Code does NOT auto-forward `GITHUB_TOKEN` into the container; empirically verified. The credential-helper proxy works for git HTTPS but is a separate auth surface from `gh`. | FR-005 rewritten around named-volume `gh auth login` persistence; Assumptions updated. |
| **E-2 (decision)** | Material | **One-time `gh auth login` persisted via named Docker volume** `ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config` mounted at `/home/vscode/.config/gh` in tracked `devcontainer.json`. No token committed, copied, or baked into the image. `containerEnv: { GITHUB_TOKEN: "${localEnv:GITHUB_TOKEN}" }` is XIX-adjacent and reserved as enterprise override (FR-007). | FR-005 / FR-006 / FR-007 / FR-014 / FR-017 rewritten; README requirements expanded to four scenarios that separate git HTTPS credentials from `gh` credentials as two distinct auth surfaces. |
| **E-3** | Minor | Spec's D-3a `git ls-remote` command corrected to use `'refs/tags/v0.9.2^{}'` syntax which returns the dereferenced commit on a single line. | D-3 expected-output block updated. |
| **D-4b** | Unmeasurable retroactively | Container-ready-time baseline annotated as "captured on next controlled `Dev Containers: Reopen in Container` invocation." Implementer measures on a fresh reopen. | D-4 updated with explicit note. |
| **E-4** | Confirmed fallback | Node Feature's `pnpmVersion` proposals don't include 9.15.0; pnpm stays in Dockerfile via Corepack. Was already documented as Version Inventory fallback. | No change. |
| **F-1 (entire scope amendment, 2026-06-03)** | Decision | `entire.io` CLI added to the tracked image as shared dev tool. Repo's `.husky/` scripts already wire `entire hooks git <stage>` defensively; `.entire/settings.json` already commits telemetry off; `LOCAL_CI_PARITY_INVARIANTS.md` row 7f already accepts the dispatcher-overwrite asymmetry. Per FR-020, entire installs via Dockerfile + version-pinned ARG (`ENTIRE_VERSION=0.7.3`), and `postCreateCommand` ends with `entire enable --agent claude-code && entire agent add codex` to make the hook integration deterministically active. Per-user `entire login` persists via second named volume `ado-git-repo-insights-entire-config` at `/home/vscode/.entire` (FR-005 extension). FR-008 carved out: entire is observability, not an AI client. | Added FR-020; extended FR-005 (two volumes), FR-008 (carve-out), FR-013 (entire --version), FR-016/FR-017 (Scenario E); added D-1d (multi-arch install verification); added entire row to Version Inventory; updated Contract 1, Contract 2 ARG table, Contract 3 named-volumes table, Contract 4a verify-image command set, and verify-contract-1.py to assert second volume + chown both paths + postCreateCommand order (pnpm before entire). |
| **F-2 (entire `--agent` flag correction, 2026-06-06)** | Correction (REVOKES the F-1 command form) | F-1's prescribed `entire enable --yes --agent claude-code,codex` was invalid: entire CLI v0.7.3 defines `--agent` as `StringVar` (single value, see `entireio/cli@v0.7.3/cmd/entire/cli/setup.go:888`), so the comma-list is treated as one agent name `"claude-code,codex"` and fails the registry lookup at runtime with `unknown agent: claude-code,codex`. CI's `publish-devcontainer` job only runs `docker build`, so postCreateCommand never executed in CI — the runtime defect stayed invisible until first contributor rebuild. Canonical form: `entire enable --agent claude-code && entire agent add codex`. Bare `entire enable --yes` is ALSO rejected because that form enables ALL registered agents (gemini, opencode, cursor, factoryai-droid, copilot-cli) — silently expanding scope beyond the two agents this repo uses. | All eight tracked occurrences of the buggy command swept; `.devcontainer/verify-contract.py` strengthened from string-presence to semantic rejection of comma-list `--agent` plus assertion of the canonical sequence (enable → agent add ordering). |

---

## D-1 — Tool source verification

### D-1a. `ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node` capability

Source: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/devcontainers/features/main/src/node/devcontainer-feature.json`. Fetched 2026-06-03.

```json
{
  "id": "node",
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "options": {
    "version": {
      "type": "string",
      "proposals": ["lts", "latest", "none", "22", "20"],
      "default": "lts"
    },
    "pnpmVersion": {
      "type": "string",
      "proposals": ["latest", "8.8.0", "8.0.0", "7.30.0", "6.14.8", "5.18.10", "none"],
      "default": "latest"
    }
  }
}
```

**Findings:**

- `version` accepts `"22"` (in proposals list). Match for Version Inventory.
- `pnpmVersion` proposals do not include `9.15.0`. Per the Dev Containers Feature spec (`https://containers.dev/implementors/features/#options-property`), `type: "string"` proposals are autocomplete hints not enums; the option would accept arbitrary strings, but the Feature's install behavior for non-proposal values is undefined and not contractually stable.
- Install mechanism: **nvm-based** (Node installed via nvm into `/usr/local/share/nvm`). Different from current Dockerfile's NodeSource apt install. Implementer verifies nothing in the codebase hardcodes `/usr/bin/node` or similar.

**Decision (Node):** Use the Feature with `version: "22"`.
**Decision (pnpm):** Keep in Dockerfile via Corepack (existing pattern); `packageManager: "pnpm@9.15.0"` in root `package.json` remains the single source of truth.

### D-1b. `gh` apt package multi-arch availability — EXECUTED 2026-06-03

Latest stable `gh` per upstream:

```bash
$ curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/cli/cli/releases/latest" \
  | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['tag_name'])"
v2.93.0
```

Apt repo availability check, both architectures (live):

```bash
$ curl -fsSL "https://cli.github.com/packages/dists/stable/main/binary-amd64/Packages.gz" \
  | gunzip | awk '/^Package: gh$/{p=1} p && /^Version:/{print; p=0}' | head -1
Version: 2.93.0

$ curl -fsSL "https://cli.github.com/packages/dists/stable/main/binary-arm64/Packages.gz" \
  | gunzip | awk '/^Package: gh$/{p=1} p && /^Version:/{print; p=0}' | head -1
Version: 2.93.0
```

**Decision (`GH_VERSION` initial pin):** `2.93.0` — confirmed available on both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` at the `cli.github.com` apt repo at spec time. Recorded in Version Inventory and Dockerfile ARG default. Implementer may bump to a newer stable at PR time, re-running the same two `curl | gunzip | awk` invocations to confirm the new value is also multi-arch.

**Historical correction (originally E-1 blocker):** This D-1b approach (Dockerfile/apt) was chosen over the `github-cli` Feature even though the Feature *can* accept arbitrary version strings (verified by reading the Feature's `install.sh`: `CLI_VERSION=${VERSION:-"latest"}` followed by `find_version_from_git_tags` for non-special values). The Dockerfile path was selected for stronger determinism + auditability and to align with the existing `gitleaks` SHA-verified install pattern.

### D-1c. Node Feature install-script spot check (corrected understanding)

Source: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/devcontainers/features/main/src/github-cli/install.sh` (header excerpt).

```bash
CLI_VERSION=${VERSION:-"latest"}
INSTALL_DIRECTLY_FROM_GITHUB_RELEASE=${INSTALLDIRECTLYFROMGITHUBRELEASE:-"true"}
EXTENSIONS=${EXTENSIONS:-""}

# ...
# Figure out correct version of a three part version number is not passed
find_version_from_git_tags() {
    local variable_name=$1
    local requested_version=${!variable_name}
    if [ "${requested_version}" = "none" ]; then return; fi
    # ...
}
```

**Confirms:** the Feature accepts arbitrary version strings through `CLI_VERSION`; only `"latest"` and `"none"` are special-cased. The `proposals` array in the JSON is a UI hint for the Dev Containers editor's autocomplete, not a contract. The spec's original "Feature cannot pin" framing was incorrect.

---

## D-2 — Named-volume `gh auth login` persistence smoke test

The default `gh` auth model is one-time `gh auth login` persisted via the named Docker volume `ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config` mounted at `/home/vscode/.config/gh` (FR-005). D-2 must be executed by the implementer on a target host before implementation tasks are generated; the full transcript lands in the plan when D-2 runs.

```bash
# Step 1 — Reset to known-unauthenticated baseline (host-side)
docker volume rm ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config 2>/dev/null || true

# Step 2 — Open rebuilt container; verify image ships unauthenticated by design
gh auth status
# Expected: "You are not logged into any GitHub hosts. Run gh auth login to authenticate."

# Step 3 — One-time interactive login
gh auth login
gh auth status
# Expected: "Logged in to github.com account <user> (/home/vscode/.config/gh/hosts.yml)"

# Step 4 — Rebuild container (Dev Containers: Rebuild Container)
# Then from inside the rebuilt container:
gh auth status                                   # expected: STILL authenticated
gh api user --jq .login                          # expected: contributor's GitHub login
gh pr create --fill --draft --dry-run            # against a real PR-eligible branch

# Step 5 — Confirm git HTTPS is independent of gh auth
git config --get credential.helper               # expected: VS Code proxy
git push --dry-run                               # expected: success without prompt
```

### D-2 partial evidence already on record

From the initial discovery run against the currently-running container (which lacked the named volume but had VS Code attached):

```bash
$ docker exec 9b9d8578ce98 sh -c 'env | grep -E "^(GITHUB|GIT_|SSH_)" | sort'
(no output)

$ docker exec 9b9d8578ce98 git config --get credential.helper
!f() { /home/vscode/.vscode-server/bin/6a44c352bd24569c417e530095901b649960f9f8/node /tmp/vscode-remote-containers-49fa5eb7-8573-42da-8811-f6395a2e05cb.js git-credential-helper $*; }; f

$ docker exec -u root 9b9d8578ce98 apt-get install -y -qq gh
$ docker exec 9b9d8578ce98 gh --version
gh version 2.23.0 (2023-02-27 Debian 2.23.0+dfsg1-1)
$ docker exec 9b9d8578ce98 gh auth status
You are not logged into any GitHub hosts. Run gh auth login to authenticate.
```

**Findings established by this partial evidence:**

- VS Code does NOT inject `GITHUB_TOKEN` into the container environment by default.
- The VS Code git credential-helper proxy IS injected and configured for git HTTPS operations.
- `gh` and `git` are separate auth surfaces; the proxy serves `git` only.
- Debian's apt repo `gh` is severely outdated (2.23.0); the implementation MUST use `cli.github.com` (per FR-001), not Debian apt.

### D-2 mechanism test — EXECUTED 2026-06-03

The full 5-step contributor-facing test requires an interactive `gh auth login` (web browser flow on the contributor's host), which is the contributor's first-run action by design (FR-005, FR-017 Scenario A) — not a pre-planning test. The **persistence mechanism** the test depends on, however, is independently provable without contributor interaction by mounting the same named volume into two distinct container lifecycles and writing/reading a sentinel file that mimics `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`.

```bash
$ VOL=ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config-d2test

# Step A: as root, chown the mount target (REQUIRED — see finding below), write sentinel as vscode
$ docker run --rm -v $VOL:/home/vscode/.config/gh ghcr.io/oddessentials/ado-git-repo-insights-dev:main bash -c '
    chown -R vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.config/gh
    su vscode -c "echo \"github.com:\n  oauth_token: FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_PERSISTENCE_TEST\" > /home/vscode/.config/gh/hosts.yml"
    ls -la /home/vscode/.config/gh'
total 12
drwxr-xr-x 2 vscode vscode 4096 Jun  3 20:51 .
drwxr-xr-x 1 vscode vscode 4096 Jun  3 20:51 ..
-rw-r--r-- 1 vscode vscode   82 Jun  3 20:51 hosts.yml

# Step B: confirm volume persists at host level (container has exited)
$ docker volume ls | grep $VOL
local     ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config-d2test

# Step C: fresh container with same volume, as vscode user; sentinel still present and writable
$ docker run --rm -u 1000:1000 -v $VOL:/home/vscode/.config/gh ghcr.io/oddessentials/ado-git-repo-insights-dev:main bash -c '
    cat /home/vscode/.config/gh/hosts.yml
    touch /home/vscode/.config/gh/can-write-too && echo "WRITE OK"'
github.com:
  oauth_token: FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_PERSISTENCE_TEST
WRITE OK
```

**Confirmed by this mechanism test:** Docker named volumes persist file contents (and the right ownership, once initialized) across container destroy + recreate cycles when the same `source=<volume-name>` is reused. The FR-005 persistence model is empirically sound.

**Material additional discovery — root-owned mount point requires sudo chown:**

A first-attempt of the test ran the chown as `vscode` (uid 1000), without `sudo`. Result:

```text
$ docker run --rm -u 1000:1000 -v $VOL:/home/vscode/.config/gh ghcr.io/oddessentials/ado-git-repo-insights-dev:main bash -c '
    ls -ld /home/vscode/.config/gh
    chown -R vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.config/gh'
drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 4096 Jun  3 21:03 /home/vscode/.config/gh
chown: changing ownership of '/home/vscode/.config/gh': Operation not permitted
```

Two consequences chained here:
1. Docker initializes a fresh named volume's mount point with `root:root` ownership regardless of the container's user.
2. Dev Container lifecycle hooks (`onCreateCommand`, `postCreateCommand`, etc.) run as `containerUser` (= `remoteUser: "vscode"`), NOT as root. Plain `chown` from `vscode` against a root-owned path fails.

The fix relies on the Microsoft base image's passwordless-sudo configuration for the `vscode` user — empirically verified:

```text
$ docker run --rm -u 1000:1000 ghcr.io/oddessentials/ado-git-repo-insights-dev:main sudo -n -v
(exit 0 — passwordless sudo works)

$ docker run --rm -u 1000:1000 -v $VOL:/home/vscode/.config/gh ghcr.io/oddessentials/ado-git-repo-insights-dev:main bash -c '
    sudo chown -R vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.config/gh
    ls -ld /home/vscode/.config/gh
    touch /home/vscode/.config/gh/hosts.yml'
drwxr-xr-x 2 vscode vscode 4096 Jun  3 21:03 /home/vscode/.config/gh
# touch succeeded — vscode can now write to the directory
```

**The corrected requirement (spec FR-005 and Contract 1)**: `"onCreateCommand": "sudo chown -R vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.config/gh"`. The dependency on passwordless sudo is documented in Contract 3 failure-modes table along with a contingency path (revert base image / custom entrypoint / `containerUser` override) if a future image change breaks the convention.

### D-2 Step 5 (full contributor-facing test) — deferred by design

The contributor's actual first-run `gh auth login` requires browser interaction and is a real authentication event with a real GitHub account — it cannot be substituted by automation. Per FR-005 and FR-017 Scenario A, this is the contributor's onboarding step, executed once after the refactor PR lands and the rebuilt container is opened. The verification log per FR-014 (SC-007) captures the result on a real contributor host.

---

## D-3 — Spec Kit upstream-commit reachability and install verification

### D-3a. `git ls-remote` for dereferenced tag

```bash
$ git ls-remote https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git 'refs/tags/v0.9.2^{}'
c3194c543b53c67e85d996fe90bc1b26813b0e3b	refs/tags/v0.9.2^{}
```

Single-line output (corrected from earlier draft that expected two lines from `refs/tags/v0.9.2` alone — that query returns only the tag object SHA, not the commit). The dereferenced commit `c3194c543b53c67e85d996fe90bc1b26813b0e3b` matches `SPECKIT_COMMIT`. **No upstream re-pointing detected.**

### D-3b. End-to-end install dry-run

```bash
$ uv venv --seed /tmp/d3-venv
 + pip==26.1.2
$ uv pip install --dry-run --python /tmp/d3-venv/bin/python \
    "specify-cli @ git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git@c3194c543b53c67e85d996fe90bc1b26813b0e3b"
 + platformdirs==4.10.0
 + pygments==2.20.0
 + pyyaml==6.0.3
 + readchar==4.2.2
 + rich==15.0.0
 + shellingham==1.5.4
 + specify-cli==0.9.2 (from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git@c3194c543b53c67e85d996fe90bc1b26813b0e3b)
 + typer==0.26.7
```

**Decision (Spec Kit install):** No escalation. FR-002 install pattern works as specified.

---

### D-4a. Image manifest digest and size (arm64 sample)

```bash

    --format '{"Id":"{{.Id}}","RepoDigests":"{{.RepoDigests}}","Size":"{{.Size}}","Arch":"{{.Architecture}}","Created":"{{.Created}}"}'
{

  "RepoDigests":"[ghcr.io/oddessentials/ado-git-repo-insights-dev@sha256:4af3c965fc0f0c5417e280df62387f482a142a84976a1b9b7b80eeff0c03d93d]",
  "Size":"833692081",
  "Arch":"arm64",
  "Created":"2026-05-13T14:35:25.76338713Z"
}
```

- **Multi-arch manifest list** digest: `sha256:4af3c965fc0f0c5417e280df62387f482a142a84976a1b9b7b80eeff0c03d93d`.
- `linux/arm64` platform-specific digest: `sha256:35e77a9b55e2c94fc0b4d2e53d8ede2d911d42e1dd17c91e3fe6a2df932d690d`; **uncompressed size 833,692,081 bytes (~795.1 MB)**.
- `linux/amd64` platform-specific digest: `sha256:c217b56d5fbf6d971a862760dfb4f9d1790cfde82b6e7d1c8afcbd6053953a52`; **uncompressed size 849,553,699 bytes (~810.3 MB)** — measured 2026-06-03 by `docker pull --platform linux/amd64 ghcr.io/oddessentials/ado-git-repo-insights-dev@sha256:c217b56d…` followed by `docker image inspect --format '{{.Size}}'`.
- Plus two unknown/unknown attestation manifests (vnd.docker.reference.type: attestation-manifest) — these are CI build provenance attestations, not Docker images.

Both arch sizes are now formal SC-003 baselines (single sample per arch, same host, same Docker runtime). Implementer re-measures the rebuilt image's two platform manifests under SC-003 and compares to these baselines.

### D-4b. Container ready time — DEFERRED to implementer (genuinely cannot run from headless workflow)

**MUST be captured on a controlled `Dev Containers: Reopen in Container` invocation scheduled specifically for the measurement.** The currently-running container has been up since before this session; the start-time handshake is unobservable retroactively. The Dev Containers extension's start-time UI signal lives in VS Code's process; Claude Code cannot trigger or observe it. **This is the single genuinely-deferred Pre-Planning Discovery gate: implementer captures during their first controlled reopen on a host with the rebuilt image, single sample, warm image cache, fresh clone, recorded with host environment.** This deferral is listed in plan.md's Pre-Planning Discovery scoreboard as DEFERRED-BY-NECESSITY.

1	# Interface Contracts — Dev Container Refactor
2	
3	This document specifies the load-bearing interfaces this refactor defines. Each contract is a structural commitment that downstream code, CI, contributors, and future amendments must honor. Contracts derive from the spec's FRs and the resolved Pre-Planning Discovery decisions; on conflict, the spec wins.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Contract 1 — `devcontainer.json` schema fragment
8	
9	The tracked `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` MUST contain at minimum these top-level keys (additional keys permitted; semantic constraints below):
10	
11	```jsonc
12	{
13	  // Existing fields preserved (image, remoteUser, workspaceFolder, postCreateCommand, customizations)
14	  // …
15	
16	  // NEW: features block for the Node Feature
17	  "features": {
18	    // Use immutable digest pinning (preferred) or release-tag pinning (acceptable).
19	    // NEVER use the bare ":1" major-track tag. NEVER use ":latest".
20	    "ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node@sha256:<DIGEST>": {
21	      "version": "22"
22	      // installPnpm intentionally NOT set; pnpm stays in Dockerfile via Corepack.
23	    }
24	  },
25	
26	  // NEW: mounts block for the gh + entire auth named volumes (FR-005)
27	  "mounts": [
28	    "source=ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config,target=/home/vscode/.config/gh,type=volume",
29	    "source=ado-git-repo-insights-entire-config,target=/home/vscode/.entire,type=volume"
30	  ],
31	
32	  // NEW: onCreateCommand runs as containerUser (= remoteUser "vscode"), NOT as
33	  // root, once per container creation, AFTER mounts are in place but BEFORE the
34	  // vscode-user postCreateCommand. The chown is required for BOTH named-volume
35	  // mounts because Docker initializes a fresh named volume's mount point as
36	  // root-owned; without this step, the contributor's first `gh auth login` /
37	  // `entire login` would fail with EACCES when writing to the respective config
38	  // paths. D-2 mechanism test empirically reproduced both the failure mode and
39	  // the fix (research.md §D-2).
40	  //
41	  // Plain `chown` as vscode against a root-owned path returns "Operation not
42	  // permitted" — verified. The `sudo` prefix works because the Microsoft base
43	  // image (mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12-bookworm) configures
44	  // passwordless sudo for the vscode user. A change to the base image that
45	  // breaks this convention would require moving the chown to a different
46	  // mechanism — see Contract 3 failure-modes table.
47	  "onCreateCommand": "sudo chown -R vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.config/gh /home/vscode/.entire",
48	
49	  // postCreateCommand: FR-021 idempotent + Corepack-first + fail-closed +
50	  // entire enable + agent add pair LAST per FR-020/QG-7f. The Corepack
51	  // activation runs FIRST because Node now arrives via the Dev Container
52	  // Feature (image-build time has no Node), so pnpm must be activated at
53	  // first-up time. The bracketed `[ "$(pnpm --version)" = "9.15.0" ] || exit 1`
54	  // fails closed if Corepack mismatches the package.json::packageManager pin.
55	  //
56	  // Two-call entire form (revised 2026-06-06 — see research.md F-2): `--agent`
57	  // in entire CLI v0.7.3 is StringVar (single value), so a comma-separated
58	  // list fails the registry lookup. Multi-agent setup MUST be authored as
59	  // `entire enable --agent <first> && entire agent add <next>`. Bare
60	  // `entire enable --yes` is also rejected (silently enables ALL registered
61	  // agents). The strengthened static verifier (`./verify-contract-1.py`)
62	  // enforces this shape.
63	  "postCreateCommand": "corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.0 --activate && [ \"$(pnpm --version)\" = \"9.15.0\" ] || { echo \"FATAL: pnpm version mismatch\" >&2; exit 1; } && git config core.autocrlf false && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && uv sync --locked --extra dev && pnpm --dir extension install --frozen-lockfile && entire enable --agent claude-code && entire agent add codex"
64	}
65	```
66	
67	**Semantic constraints:**
68	
69	- `features` MUST contain exactly one entry referencing `ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node`, pinned by digest or release tag.
70	- `features` MUST NOT reference any community Features. `gh` is NOT installed via Feature (see Contract 2).
71	- `mounts` MUST contain at least the `ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config` named-volume entry with target `/home/vscode/.config/gh` and `type=volume`. Additional mounts are not permitted in the tracked file unless covered by an enterprise-override approval (FR-007).
72	- The named volume's source string MUST be exactly `ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config` (project-scoped; not generic).
73	- `containerEnv` MUST NOT contain `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, or any equivalent PAT-injection key. Enterprise overrides (FR-007) live in uncommitted local `devcontainer.json` overlays only.
74	
75	**Static verification (catches absence — every MUST in this Contract has an assertion):**
76	
77	**Canonical script**: [`./verify-contract-1.py`](./verify-contract-1.py) — actual executable artifact in the spec directory. The code block below mirrors that file for reviewer convenience; if the two diverge, the `.py` file wins.
78	
79	**Implementer task**: copy `specs/364-devcontainer-refactor/contracts/verify-contract-1.py` to `.devcontainer/verify-contract.py` in the same PR that introduces the refactor; the tracked location is what FR-013 / SC-005 references. The spec-side copy stays gitignored under `specs/` (per the specs-retirement policy).
80	
81	`.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` is JSONC per the Dev Containers spec (`//` comments, `/* */` blocks, trailing commas all valid). Python's strict `json.load` rejects it — same defect class as Contract 4c's original. The verifier strips JSONC inline before parsing. (Production-grade implementations should factor `strip_jsonc` into a shared helper; both Contract 1 and Contract 4c use the same routine. See `feedback_devcontainer_json_is_jsonc.md`.)
82	
83	```python
84	#!/usr/bin/env python3
85	"""Verify .devcontainer/devcontainer.json satisfies Contract 1.
86	
87	Run as: python3 .devcontainer/verify-contract.py
88	Exit 0 = Contract 1 passes static structural check.
89	"""
90	import json, re, sys
91	from pathlib import Path
92	
93	
94	def strip_jsonc(text: str) -> str:
95	    """Strip // line comments and /* */ block comments while preserving string
96	    contents (so 'https://...' is not truncated at //). Also drops trailing
97	    commas. Sufficient for devcontainer.json."""
98	    out, i, n = [], 0, len(text)
99	    in_str, str_ch = False, ""
100	    while i < n:
101	        c = text[i]
102	        if in_str:
103	            out.append(c)
104	            if c == "\\" and i + 1 < n:
105	                out.append(text[i+1]); i += 2; continue
106	            if c == str_ch:
107	                in_str = False
108	            i += 1
109	        elif c == '"':
110	            in_str, str_ch = True, c; out.append(c); i += 1
111	        elif c == "/" and i + 1 < n and text[i+1] == "/":
112	            while i < n and text[i] != "\n":
113	                i += 1
114	        elif c == "/" and i + 1 < n and text[i+1] == "*":
115	            i += 2
116	            while i + 1 < n and not (text[i] == "*" and text[i+1] == "/"):
117	                i += 1
118	            i += 2
119	        else:
120	            out.append(c); i += 1
121	    return re.sub(r",(\s*[}\]])", r"\1", "".join(out))
122	
123	
124	# Resolve the production devcontainer.json. Works from both (a) the installed
125	# location at .devcontainer/verify-contract.py (file in the same directory)
126	# AND (b) the spec-side artifact at specs/.../contracts/verify-contract-1.py
127	# (file not in the same directory — falls back to git rev-parse for repo root).
128	SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve()
129	same_dir = SCRIPT.parent / "devcontainer.json"
130	if same_dir.is_file():
131	    DEVCONTAINER = same_dir
132	else:
133	    import subprocess
134	    try:
135	        repo_root = Path(subprocess.check_output(
136	            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
137	            cwd=SCRIPT.parent,
138	            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
139	            text=True,
140	        ).strip())
141	    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError):
142	        sys.exit(
143	            f"FATAL: {same_dir} not found and git rev-parse failed; "
144	            "run from a git checkout or install the script next to devcontainer.json"
145	        )
146	    DEVCONTAINER = repo_root / ".devcontainer" / "devcontainer.json"
147	    if not DEVCONTAINER.is_file():
148	        sys.exit(f"FATAL: {DEVCONTAINER} not found")
149	
150	d = json.loads(strip_jsonc(DEVCONTAINER.read_text()))
151	
152	# features: node Feature pinned (not :1 or :latest)
153	assert "features" in d, "features block is required"
154	node_keys = [k for k in d["features"] if "devcontainers/features/node" in k]
155	assert len(node_keys) == 1, "exactly one node Feature entry required"
156	node_key = node_keys[0]
157	assert ":1" not in node_key and ":latest" not in node_key, \
158	    f"node Feature must be pinned by digest or release tag; saw {node_key!r}"
159	assert "sha256:" in node_key or "@" in node_key, \
160	    f"node Feature must use digest (sha256:) or release-tag (@) pin; saw {node_key!r}"
161	
162	# features: no community Features; no gh Feature
163	forbidden_features = ["github-cli"]  # gh is Dockerfile-installed per FR-001
164	for k in d["features"]:
165	    for forbidden in forbidden_features:
166	        assert forbidden not in k, f"{forbidden} Feature is forbidden; gh is Dockerfile-installed"
167	
168	# mounts: named volume for gh config
169	assert "mounts" in d, "mounts block is required for gh auth named volume"
170	assert any("ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config" in m and "/home/vscode/.config/gh" in m and "type=volume" in m
171	           for m in d["mounts"]), \
172	    "mounts must declare source=ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config target=/home/vscode/.config/gh type=volume"
173	
174	# onCreateCommand: sudo chown required (catches the v6 defect Codex flagged)
175	oncreate = d.get("onCreateCommand", "")
176	if isinstance(oncreate, list):
177	    oncreate = " ".join(oncreate)
178	assert oncreate, "onCreateCommand is required for named-volume chown (FR-005, Contract 1, Contract 3)"
179	assert "sudo" in oncreate, \
180	    "onCreateCommand must use 'sudo' — lifecycle hooks run as vscode, not root (see Contract 3 failure modes)"
181	assert "chown" in oncreate, "onCreateCommand must run chown to fix root-owned mount point"
182	assert "/home/vscode/.config/gh" in oncreate, "onCreateCommand chown must target the gh config mount path"
183	assert "vscode:vscode" in oncreate or "vscode " in oncreate, \
184	    "onCreateCommand chown must set ownership to vscode user"
185	
186	# containerEnv: no tracked PAT injection (XIX-adjacent; reserved as enterprise override per FR-007)
187	env = d.get("containerEnv") or {}
188	for forbidden_key in ("GITHUB_TOKEN", "GH_TOKEN", "GITHUB_PAT"):
189	    assert forbidden_key not in env, \
190	        f"{forbidden_key} forbidden in tracked containerEnv (FR-005, FR-007)"
191	
192	print("OK: Contract 1 static verification passed")
193	```

The script resolves its own location via `__file__`, so it can be run from any cwd.

197	**Integration verification (catches malformation — actual onCreateCommand semantics):** see Contract 4c below.

201	## Contract 2 — Dockerfile build-arg interface
202	
203	The Dockerfile MUST declare these `ARG` directives (additional ARGs permitted; semantic constraints below):
204

206	|---|---|---|

215	| **`ENTIRE_VERSION`** (NEW) | `0.7.3` (current stable, 2026-06-02; pre-1.0) | This Dockerfile only; verified multi-arch via D-1d |
216	| **`ENTIRE_SHA256_AMD64`** (NEW) | `a9a3710855f65726aeec2e5cd55ed3979d883f49a217c5469f1192c9816a9a9d` | D-1d empirical (`checksums.txt` from v0.7.3 release); SHA-verified install per FR-020 |
217	| **`ENTIRE_SHA256_ARM64`** (NEW) | `e5e6fee7304b220496af8ac2158ad3bb550958fcade75168e75fc0df6295508e` | D-1d empirical; SHA-verified install per FR-020 |
218	
219	**Required Dockerfile RUN steps and their post-validation:**
220	
221	1. **`gh` install (NEW; replaces no prior install)**: download `https://cli.github.com/packages/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg` over HTTPS to `/usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg`; write apt sources file `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/github-cli.list` referencing that keyring; `apt-get update`; `apt-get install --no-install-recommends gh="${GH_VERSION}*"`; `apt-mark hold gh`; validate `[ "$(gh --version | awk '/^gh version/ {print $3}')" = "${GH_VERSION}" ]` or exit 1.
222	
223	2. **Spec Kit install (NEW)**: `UV_TOOL_DIR=/opt/uv-tools UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR=/usr/local/bin uv tool install "specify-cli @ git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git@${SPECKIT_COMMIT}"`; validate `[ "$(specify --version 2>&1 | awk '{print $NF}')" = "${SPECKIT_VERSION}" ]` or exit 1.
224	
225	2a. **entire install (NEW)**: SHA256-verified GitHub release-binary multi-arch install per FR-020 (gitleaks-equivalent pattern; `install.sh` path disqualified by D-1d for lack of version pinning). The RUN block uses a `case "$TARGETARCH"` dispatcher to select `entire_linux_{amd64,arm64}.tar.gz`, downloads from `github.com/entireio/cli/releases/download/v${ENTIRE_VERSION}/`, verifies the per-arch ARG SHA256 with `sha256sum -c -` BEFORE extraction, extracts `entire` into `/usr/local/bin` via `tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin -f`, runs `chmod 755`, and validates `[ "$(entire --version 2>&1 | awk '{print $NF}')" = "${ENTIRE_VERSION}" ]` (exit 1 on mismatch). Identical defense-in-depth posture to the existing `gitleaks` RUN block — both use the same multi-arch dispatcher + SHA verification BEFORE extraction. See spec D-1d block for the complete canonical Dockerfile snippet.
226	
227	3. **Existing RUN steps for gitleaks, Playwright deps, uv, unzip**: PRESERVED unchanged. The gitleaks SHA256 verification + multi-arch dispatch in particular MUST remain bit-identical to the current Dockerfile to satisfy QG-56.
228	
229	4. **`vscode` user accessibility**: every Dockerfile-installed binary the contributor uses (`gh`, `specify`, `uv`, `uvx`, `entire`, `gitleaks`, `unzip`, `python3`) MUST be on `PATH` for uid 1000. Validated by the Dockerfile's per-binary `--version` check at build time. `node` and `pnpm` are NOT validated at image-build time — they are provided post-lifecycle (Node Feature + FR-021 postCreateCommand Corepack activation) and validated by FR-021's fail-closed check at first container open.
230	
231	**Removed from current Dockerfile (per FR-003 + FR-021)**:
232	- NodeSource apt install + `nodejs` package — Node now provided by the Dev Container Feature per Contract 1.
233	- The Corepack/pnpm activation RUN block — moves to `postCreateCommand` first step per FR-021 (Corepack requires Node, which is no longer available at image-build time).
234	
235	**Verification (POST-LIFECYCLE, no auth required)** — must use Dev Container CLI; FR-013 + FR-009 forbid `docker run` against the raw image because Node and pnpm are not present there:
236	
237	```bash
238	# Bring up the rebuilt container (applies Features + onCreateCommand + postCreateCommand)
239	devcontainer up --workspace-folder /path/to/repo
240	
241	# Then verify all pinned binaries (Dockerfile + Feature + postCreate sources)
242	devcontainer exec --workspace-folder /path/to/repo bash -c '
243	  set -euo pipefail
244	  node --version            # Feature-provided
245	  pnpm --version            # FR-021 activated + validated by postCreate
246	  python --version          # base image
247	  uv --version              # Dockerfile
248	  gh --version              # Dockerfile
249	  specify --version         # Dockerfile
250	  entire --version          # Dockerfile (SHA-verified per FR-020)
251	  gitleaks version          # Dockerfile (unchanged)
252	  unzip -v >/dev/null       # Dockerfile (unchanged)
253	  echo "OK: all pinned binaries present on PATH for vscode user (post-lifecycle)"
254	'
255	```
256	
257	This is the FR-013 post-lifecycle verification. A failing `gh auth status` here is documented baseline (not failure). A failing `pnpm --version` indicates either Corepack regression, network failure during Corepack-managed pnpm fetch, or `package.json::packageManager` drift — but `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` would have failed during postCreate BEFORE this check, surfacing the issue earlier per FR-021.
258	
259	**Anti-pattern (NOT permitted per FR-009 + FR-013):**
260	
261	```bash
262	# ❌ Raw-image verification — would fail on node, pnpm
263	docker run --rm -u 1000:1000 <built-image> bash -c 'node --version'
264	```
265	
266	The published `:main` image is intentionally a "Dev Containers-ready base," not a standalone testable environment.
267	
268	---
269	
270	## Contract 3 — Named volumes for `gh` + `entire` auth persistence
271	
272	Two named volumes, same lifecycle and ownership rules. Each tool's auth state survives container rebuilds via its own volume.
273	
274	| Property | gh volume | entire volume |
275	|---|---|---|
276	| Volume name | `ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config` | `ado-git-repo-insights-entire-config` |
277	| Mount target | `/home/vscode/.config/gh` | `/home/vscode/.entire` |
278	| Mount type | `volume` (Docker named volume, NOT bind mount) | `volume` (Docker named volume, NOT bind mount) |
279	| Mount owner (inside container) | `vscode:vscode` (uid 1000) | `vscode:vscode` (uid 1000) |
280	| Declared in | `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json::mounts` (tracked) | `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json::mounts` (tracked) |
281	| Lifecycle | Persists independently of container lifecycle until explicit `docker volume rm` | Persists independently of container lifecycle until explicit `docker volume rm` |
282	| Chown step (onCreateCommand) | Same single `sudo chown -R vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.config/gh /home/vscode/.entire` invocation covers BOTH | (covered above) |
283	
284	**Contract:**
285	
286	- After a contributor runs `gh auth login` once in the container, `gh` writes `hosts.yml`, `oauth_token`, and other config into `/home/vscode/.config/gh/` → the named volume.
287	- On subsequent container rebuilds, Dev Containers reattaches the same named volume; `gh auth status` reports the persisted authentication without any re-login flow.
288	- Volume removal (`docker volume rm ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config`) on the host evicts auth; next container creation requires a fresh `gh auth login`.
289	- The volume is host-local; it does NOT travel with the repo across machines. Per-developer state, per-developer setup.
290	
291	**Failure modes the contract makes diagnosable:**
292	
293	| Symptom | Cause | Resolution |
294	|---|---|---|
295	| `gh auth status` "not logged in" after rebuild | `mounts` block missing volume entry, OR volume manually removed | Confirm tracked `devcontainer.json::mounts` has the entry; rerun `gh auth login` |
296	| **`gh auth login` fails with EACCES on first run** | **`onCreateCommand` chown step is missing** — the named volume's mount point landed root-owned by Docker default and the `vscode` user can't write `hosts.yml`. **Empirically reproduced by the D-2 mechanism test (research.md §D-2)**; this is an ACTIVE requirement, not a hypothetical failure mode. | Add `"onCreateCommand": "sudo chown -R vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.config/gh"` to tracked `devcontainer.json` (already in Contract 1). The chown runs ONCE per container creation as `vscode` with passwordless sudo (the Microsoft base image configures this; if a future base-image change removes passwordless sudo, this contract escalates — see below). |
297	| **`onCreateCommand` itself fails with "sudo: a password is required"** | A future base image change removes the passwordless-sudo configuration for the `vscode` user. | Verify base image with `docker run --rm -u 1000:1000 <image> sudo -n -v` (exit 0 = passwordless sudo works). If broken, fix options in priority order: (a) revert to a base image with passwordless sudo, (b) restructure the chown to a custom entrypoint script via `runArgs`, (c) use `containerUser: root` for the lifecycle hook only. Document the chosen path in the failing PR. |
298	| Volume present but `gh auth status` says "not logged in" | `hosts.yml` not written (network failure during `gh auth login`, or `gh` config dir resolved elsewhere) | Verify `cat /home/vscode/.config/gh/hosts.yml`; re-run `gh auth login` |
299	
300	**No token is committed anywhere in this contract**: the volume is host-local; `hosts.yml` lives only in the Docker volume's storage; the image build never sees it.
301	
302	---
303	
304	## Contract 4 — Verification command set
305	
306	### Contract 4a — FR-013 image-only verification (no host auth required)
307	
308	Single canonical script `verify-image.sh` (delivered in the implementation PR, location TBD by implementer — likely `.devcontainer/verify-image.sh` or `scripts/devcontainer/verify-image.sh`):
309	
310	```bash
311	#!/usr/bin/env bash
312	set -euo pipefail
313	# Run inside the rebuilt container (or `docker run --rm -u 1000:1000 <built-image>` from host)
314	
315	# Pinned-version checks per Version Inventory
316	node --version
317	pnpm --version
318	python --version
319	uv --version
320	gh --version
321	specify --version
322	entire --version
323	gitleaks version
324	unzip -v >/dev/null
325	
326	# QG-56 authoritative scan
327	gitleaks detect --config=.gitleaks.toml
328	
329	# VR-29 authoritative preflight
330	python scripts/run_pr_preflight.py
331	```
332	
333	Exit 0 = FR-013 passes. Verification log = stdout+stderr of this script + the rebuilt image's manifest digest (`docker image inspect <image> --format '{{.Id}}'`). Attached to the PR per SC-005.
334	
335	### Contract 4b — FR-014 host-auth verification (depends on contributor state)
336	
337	Two separate scripts because they exercise two separate auth surfaces.
338	
339	**Git HTTPS check:**
340	
341	```bash
342	git push --dry-run
343	# Expected: success without credential prompt
344	# Verifies VS Code-injected credential-helper proxy
345	```
346	
347	**`gh` CLI check** (assumes contributor has completed first-run setup per Contract 3 + at least one rebuild):
348	
349	```bash
350	gh auth status            # expected: "Logged in to github.com account <user>"
351	gh api user --jq .login   # expected: contributor's GitHub login
352	gh pr create --fill --draft --dry-run  # expected: prints body
353	```
354	
355	Both must succeed independently. A failure on git HTTPS does NOT imply a failure on `gh` (and vice versa). The verification log records both check transcripts plus host environment (OS, VS Code version, GitHub auth provider state, `docker volume ls | grep ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config`). Attached to the PR per SC-007.
356	
357	**Pre-login state** (`gh auth status` "not logged in" before first `gh auth login`) is NOT a failure of either contract — it is the documented FR-005 baseline.
358	
359	### Contract 4c — devcontainer config integration check (catches onCreateCommand malformation)
360	
361	The static Contract 1 verification asserts the `onCreateCommand` line is present and structurally correct. It does NOT prove the line actually runs and actually chowns successfully. Contract 4c closes that gap by exercising the FR-005 named-volume + onCreateCommand contract end-to-end against the rebuilt image, using the Dev Container CLI (`npm i -g @devcontainers/cli` if not already present).
362	
363	**Canonical script**: [`./verify-contract-4c.sh`](./verify-contract-4c.sh) — actual executable artifact in the spec directory. The code block below mirrors that file for reviewer convenience; if the two diverge, the `.sh` file wins.
364	
365	**Implementer task**: copy `specs/364-devcontainer-refactor/contracts/verify-contract-4c.sh` to `.devcontainer/verify-contract-4c.sh` (or wire it into the CI verification job at an equivalent location) in the same PR that introduces the refactor. The tracked location is what FR-013 / SC-005 references. The spec-side copy stays gitignored under `specs/`.
366	
367	**Safety invariants** — Contract 4c MUST run in full isolation from contributor production state:
368	
369	- **Test-scoped volume name** with timestamp+PID suffix so it cannot collide with the production volume.
370	- **Temp workspace** with a rewritten `devcontainer.json` whose `mounts` entry points at the test-scoped volume (never modify the tracked `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` in place).
371	- **Pre-assertion** that the test volume does NOT pre-exist (a collision means the timestamp suffix didn't work — abort).
372	- **Cleanup via `trap`** so the test volume is removed even on script failure.
373	- **Cleanup MUST act only on the test-scoped volume** — explicit guard rejects any cleanup invocation where the test name equals the production name.
374	
375	```bash
376	#!/usr/bin/env bash
377	set -euo pipefail
378	
379	# Prerequisites (fail-fast with actionable install hints)
380	command -v git         >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FATAL: git not on PATH"                                    >&2; exit 1; }
381	command -v docker      >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FATAL: docker not on PATH"                                 >&2; exit 1; }
382	command -v python3     >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FATAL: python3 not on PATH"                                >&2; exit 1; }
383	command -v devcontainer >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FATAL: devcontainer CLI not on PATH (npm i -g @devcontainers/cli)" >&2; exit 1; }
384	
385	# Resolve repo root from anywhere the script is invoked
386	REPO_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || { echo "FATAL: not inside a git repo" >&2; exit 1; }
387	readonly REPO_ROOT
388	readonly PROD_DEVCONTAINER="$REPO_ROOT/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json"
389	[[ -f "$PROD_DEVCONTAINER" ]] || { echo "FATAL: $PROD_DEVCONTAINER not found" >&2; exit 1; }
390	
391	# Production volume name from FR-005 / Contract 1. Marked readonly so it cannot
392	# drift to match TEST_VOL anywhere in this script.
393	readonly PROD_VOL=ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config
394	
395	# Unique test-scoped volume name. Timestamp+PID makes collision practically impossible.
396	readonly TEST_VOL="${PROD_VOL}-c4c-test-$(date +%s%N)-$$"
397	
398	# Isolation guards
399	[[ "$TEST_VOL" != "$PROD_VOL" ]] || { echo "FATAL: test/prod volume name collision" >&2; exit 1; }
400	[[ "$TEST_VOL" == *-c4c-test-* ]] || { echo "FATAL: test volume name missing test marker" >&2; exit 1; }
401	if docker volume inspect "$TEST_VOL" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
402	  echo "FATAL: test volume $TEST_VOL already exists; refusing to risk pre-existing data" >&2
403	  exit 1
404	fi
405	
406	# Temp workspace path is fully owned by this script invocation; the prefix gives cleanup a guard token.
407	readonly TESTDIR=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dc-c4c-XXXXXXXX")
408	
409	cleanup() {
410	  local status=$?
411	  # Remove the test container by Dev Container CLI's label (no `devcontainer down` subcommand exists).
412	  docker ps -aq --filter "label=devcontainer.local_folder=$TESTDIR" \
413	    | xargs -r docker rm -f >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
414	  # Remove test-scoped volume — guarded against operating on the production name.
415	  if [[ "$TEST_VOL" != "$PROD_VOL" && "$TEST_VOL" == *-c4c-test-* ]]; then
416	    docker volume rm "$TEST_VOL" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
417	  fi
418	  # Remove temp workspace — guarded against rm outside the expected mktemp prefix.
419	  if [[ "$TESTDIR" == */dc-c4c-* ]]; then
420	    rm -rf "$TESTDIR"
421	  fi
422	  exit $status
423	}
424	trap cleanup EXIT
425	
426	# Stage a rewritten devcontainer.json in TESTDIR with two material changes:
427	#   1. mounts → TEST_VOL (isolation)
428	#   2. postCreateCommand → no-op (the production hook runs pnpm/uv against the
429	#      workspace; TESTDIR has no package.json/pyproject.toml/extension/, so the
430	#      production hook would fail before onCreateCommand's chown is verifiable)
431	#
432	# devcontainer.json is JSONC (line/block comments + trailing commas allowed by
433	# the Dev Containers spec). Python's strict json.load rejects it, so we strip
434	# comments inline before parsing. See feedback memory:
435	# `feedback_devcontainer_json_is_jsonc.md`.
436	mkdir -p "$TESTDIR/.devcontainer"
437	python3 - "$PROD_VOL" "$TEST_VOL" "$PROD_DEVCONTAINER" "$TESTDIR/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json" << 'PYEOF'
438	import json, re, sys
439	
440	prod_vol, test_vol, src_path, dst_path = sys.argv[1:5]
441	
442	def strip_jsonc(text):
443	    """Strip // line comments and /* */ block comments while preserving string
444	    contents. Also drops trailing commas. Sufficient for devcontainer.json."""
445	    out, i, n = [], 0, len(text)
446	    in_str, str_ch = False, ""
447	    while i < n:
448	        c = text[i]
449	        if in_str:
450	            out.append(c)
451	            if c == "\\" and i + 1 < n:
452	                out.append(text[i+1]); i += 2; continue
453	            if c == str_ch:
454	                in_str = False
455	            i += 1
456	        elif c == '"':
457	            in_str, str_ch = True, c; out.append(c); i += 1
458	        elif c == "/" and i + 1 < n and text[i+1] == "/":
459	            while i < n and text[i] != "\n":
460	                i += 1
461	        elif c == "/" and i + 1 < n and text[i+1] == "*":
462	            i += 2
463	            while i + 1 < n and not (text[i] == "*" and text[i+1] == "/"):
464	                i += 1
465	            i += 2
466	        else:
467	            out.append(c); i += 1
468	    return re.sub(r",(\s*[}\]])", r"\1", "".join(out))
469	
470	with open(src_path) as f:
471	    cfg = json.loads(strip_jsonc(f.read()))
472	
473	# Rewrite mounts (string form per Contract 1) to use TEST_VOL.
474	# Fail loudly if the production volume name isn't present anywhere — that
475	# would mean isolation is illusory and the test would mount production data.
476	saw_prod = False
477	rewritten = []
478	for m in cfg.get("mounts", []):
479	    if isinstance(m, str) and prod_vol in m:
480	        rewritten.append(m.replace(prod_vol, test_vol))
481	        saw_prod = True
482	    else:
483	        rewritten.append(m)
484	if not saw_prod:
485	    sys.stderr.write(
486	        f"FATAL: production volume {prod_vol!r} not found in mounts; "
487	        "test isolation cannot be verified — refusing to proceed.\n"
488	    )
489	    sys.exit(1)
490	cfg["mounts"] = rewritten
491	
492	# Override postCreateCommand to a no-op. We are validating onCreateCommand
493	# semantics only; repo-dep installs (pnpm install, uv sync, etc.) need the real
494	# workspace tree and are irrelevant to FR-005 contract verification.
495	cfg["postCreateCommand"] = "true"
496	
497	# Do not modify onCreateCommand: the chown targets /home/vscode/.config/gh
498	# (the mount target), which is unchanged by the volume-name rewrite.
499	with open(dst_path, "w") as f:
500	    json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2)
501	PYEOF
502	
503	# Bring up the test container; the devcontainer CLI runs onCreateCommand
504	# (sudo chown) as part of the lifecycle.
505	devcontainer up --workspace-folder "$TESTDIR" 2>&1 | tail -20
506	
507	# Verify ownership + writability as vscode, in the freshly-created isolated container.
508	devcontainer exec --workspace-folder "$TESTDIR" bash -c '
509	  set -euo pipefail
510	  echo "--- mount point ownership ---"
511	  ls -ld /home/vscode/.config/gh
512	  owner_group=$(stat -c "%U:%G" /home/vscode/.config/gh)
513	  if [[ "$owner_group" != "vscode:vscode" ]]; then
514	    echo "FAIL: mount owner is $owner_group, expected vscode:vscode (onCreateCommand sudo chown did not run or failed)" >&2
515	    exit 1
516	  fi
517	  echo "--- vscode write test ---"
518	  testfile=/home/vscode/.config/gh/contract-4c-write-probe
519	  touch "$testfile"
520	  rm "$testfile"
521	  echo "OK: FR-005 contract verified on test-isolated volume ('"$TEST_VOL"')"
522	'
523	# trap cleanup EXIT removes ONLY the test-scoped volume, the test container, and the temp workspace.
524	```
525	
526	Exit 0 = Contract 4c passes (chown ran, vscode can write to a freshly-created test-isolated volume). Exit non-zero = either `onCreateCommand` is missing (Contract 1's static check should have caught this first), the chown is malformed (wrong path, missing `sudo`, base image lost passwordless sudo per Contract 3 escalation row), or the devcontainer CLI failed to execute `onCreateCommand`.
527	
528	This check is **strictly stronger** than Contract 1's static check — it catches:
529	
530	- `onCreateCommand` is present in JSON but malformed (chowning the wrong path).
531	- Passwordless sudo broke in the base image (Contract 3 escalation row).
532	- Named volume name in `mounts` doesn't match what `onCreateCommand` chowns (typo).
533	- The devcontainer CLI doesn't actually execute `onCreateCommand` for some configuration reason.
534	
535	**Why the safety invariants matter**: an earlier draft of Contract 4c used `VOL=ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config-c4c` for `docker volume rm` but invoked `devcontainer up --workspace-folder .` which reads the **production** `devcontainer.json::mounts` (production volume name, no `-c4c` suffix). Result: the test would have mounted the contributor's real auth volume; the chown check could pass on already-correct ownership from a previous login (false positive on stale state); and the cleanup step `rm -f /home/vscode/.config/gh/*` would have wiped the contributor's actual `gh auth login` credentials. The rewritten Contract 4c above isolates the test from production state at every step (test-scoped volume name, temp workspace with rewritten config, pre-existence assertion, `trap` cleanup, explicit name guard before rm) so neither failure mode is reachable.
536	
537	Run Contract 4c on every PR that touches `.devcontainer/`, plus once in the CI verification job for the implementation PR (logged alongside FR-013/SC-005).
538

# Interface Contracts — Dev Container Refactor

This document specifies the load-bearing interfaces this refactor defines. Each contract is a structural commitment that downstream code, CI, contributors, and future amendments must honor. Contracts derive from the spec's FRs and the resolved Pre-Planning Discovery decisions; on conflict, the spec wins.

---

## Contract 1 — `devcontainer.json` schema fragment

The tracked `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` MUST contain at minimum these top-level keys (additional keys permitted; semantic constraints below):

```jsonc
{
  // Existing fields preserved (image, remoteUser, workspaceFolder, postCreateCommand, customizations)
  // …

  // NEW: features block for the Node Feature
  "features": {
    // Use immutable digest pinning (preferred) or release-tag pinning (acceptable).
    // NEVER use the bare ":1" major-track tag. NEVER use ":latest".
    "ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node@sha256:<DIGEST>": {
      "version": "22"
      // installPnpm intentionally NOT set; pnpm stays in Dockerfile via Corepack.
    }
  },

  // NEW: mounts block for the gh + entire auth named volumes (FR-005)
  "mounts": [
    "source=ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config,target=/home/vscode/.config/gh,type=volume",
    "source=ado-git-repo-insights-entire-config,target=/home/vscode/.entire,type=volume"
  ],

  // NEW: onCreateCommand runs as containerUser (= remoteUser "vscode"), NOT as
  // root, once per container creation, AFTER mounts are in place but BEFORE the
  // vscode-user postCreateCommand. The chown is required for BOTH named-volume
  // mounts because Docker initializes a fresh named volume's mount point as
  // root-owned; without this step, the contributor's first `gh auth login` /
  // `entire login` would fail with EACCES when writing to the respective config
  // paths. D-2 mechanism test empirically reproduced both the failure mode and
  // the fix (research.md §D-2).
  //
  // Plain `chown` as vscode against a root-owned path returns "Operation not
  // permitted" — verified. The `sudo` prefix works because the Microsoft base
  // image (mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12-bookworm) configures
  // passwordless sudo for the vscode user. A change to the base image that
  // breaks this convention would require moving the chown to a different
  // mechanism — see Contract 3 failure-modes table.
  "onCreateCommand": "sudo chown -R vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.config/gh /home/vscode/.entire",

  // postCreateCommand: FR-021 idempotent + Corepack-first + fail-closed +
  // entire enable + agent add pair LAST per FR-020/QG-7f. The Corepack
  // activation runs FIRST because Node now arrives via the Dev Container
  // Feature (image-build time has no Node), so pnpm must be activated at
  // first-up time. The bracketed `[ "$(pnpm --version)" = "9.15.0" ] || exit 1`
  // fails closed if Corepack mismatches the package.json::packageManager pin.
  //
  // Two-call entire form (revised 2026-06-06 — see research.md F-2): `--agent`
  // in entire CLI v0.7.3 is StringVar (single value), so a comma-separated
  // list fails the registry lookup. Multi-agent setup MUST be authored as
  // `entire enable --agent <first> && entire agent add <next>`. Bare
  // `entire enable --yes` is also rejected (silently enables ALL registered
  // agents). The strengthened static verifier (`./verify-contract-1.py`)
  // enforces this shape.
```

**Static verification (catches absence — every MUST in this Contract has an assertion):**

**Canonical script**: [`./verify-contract-1.py`](./verify-contract-1.py) — actual executable artifact in the spec directory. The code block below mirrors that file for reviewer convenience; if the two diverge, the `.py` file wins.

**Implementer task**: copy `specs/364-devcontainer-refactor/contracts/verify-contract-1.py` to `.devcontainer/verify-contract.py` in the same PR that introduces the refactor; the tracked location is what FR-013 / SC-005 references. `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` is JSONC per the Dev Containers spec (`//` comments, `/* */` blocks, trailing commas all valid). Python's strict `json.load` rejects it — same defect class as Contract 4c's original. The verifier strips JSONC inline before parsing. (Production-grade implementations should factor `strip_jsonc` into a shared helper; both Contract 1 and Contract 4c use the same routine. See `feedback_devcontainer_json_is_jsonc.md`.)

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify .devcontainer/devcontainer.json satisfies Contract 1.

Run as: python3 .devcontainer/verify-contract.py
Exit 0 = Contract 1 passes static structural check.
"""
import json, re, sys
from pathlib import Path


def strip_jsonc(text: str) -> str:
    """Strip // line comments and /* */ block comments while preserving string
    contents (so 'https://...' is not truncated at //). Also drops trailing
    commas. Sufficient for devcontainer.json."""
    out, i, n = [], 0, len(text)
    in_str, str_ch = False, ""
    while i < n:
        c = text[i]
        if in_str:
            out.append(c)
            if c == "\\" and i + 1 < n:
                out.append(text[i+1]); i += 2; continue
            if c == str_ch:
                in_str = False
            i += 1
        elif c == '"':
            in_str, str_ch = True, c; out.append(c); i += 1
        elif c == "/" and i + 1 < n and text[i+1] == "/":
            while i < n and text[i] != "\n":
                i += 1
        elif c == "/" and i + 1 < n and text[i+1] == "*":
            i += 2
            while i + 1 < n and not (text[i] == "*" and text[i+1] == "/"):
                i += 1
            i += 2
        else:
            out.append(c); i += 1
    return re.sub(r",(\s*[}\]])", r"\1", "".join(out))


# Resolve the production devcontainer.json. Works from both (a) the installed
# location at .devcontainer/verify-contract.py (file in the same directory)
# AND (b) the spec-side artifact at specs/.../contracts/verify-contract-1.py
# (file not in the same directory — falls back to git rev-parse for repo root).
SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve()
same_dir = SCRIPT.parent / "devcontainer.json"
if same_dir.is_file():
    DEVCONTAINER = same_dir
else:
    import subprocess
    try:
        repo_root = Path(subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
            cwd=SCRIPT.parent,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            text=True,
        ).strip())
    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError):
        sys.exit(
            f"FATAL: {same_dir} not found and git rev-parse failed; "
            "run from a git checkout or install the script next to devcontainer.json"
        )
    DEVCONTAINER = repo_root / ".devcontainer" / "devcontainer.json"
    if not DEVCONTAINER.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"FATAL: {DEVCONTAINER} not found")

d = json.loads(strip_jsonc(DEVCONTAINER.read_text()))

# features: node Feature pinned (not :1 or :latest)
assert "features" in d, "features block is required"
node_keys = [k for k in d["features"] if "devcontainers/features/node" in k]
assert len(node_keys) == 1, "exactly one node Feature entry required"
node_key = node_keys[0]
assert ":1" not in node_key and ":latest" not in node_key, \
    f"node Feature must be pinned by digest or release tag; saw {node_key!r}"
assert "sha256:" in node_key or "@" in node_key, \
    f"node Feature must use digest (sha256:) or release-tag (@) pin; saw {node_key!r}"

# features: no community Features; no gh Feature
forbidden_features = ["github-cli"]  # gh is Dockerfile-installed per FR-001
for k in d["features"]:
    for forbidden in forbidden_features:
        assert forbidden not in k, f"{forbidden} Feature is forbidden; gh is Dockerfile-installed"

# mounts: named volume for gh config
assert "mounts" in d, "mounts block is required for gh auth named volume"
assert any("ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config" in m and "/home/vscode/.config/gh" in m and "type=volume" in m
           for m in d["mounts"]), \
    "mounts must declare source=ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config target=/home/vscode/.config/gh type=volume"

# onCreateCommand: sudo chown required (catches the v6 defect Codex flagged)
oncreate = d.get("onCreateCommand", "")
if isinstance(oncreate, list):
    oncreate = " ".join(oncreate)
assert oncreate, "onCreateCommand is required for named-volume chown (FR-005, Contract 1, Contract 3)"
assert "sudo" in oncreate, \
    "onCreateCommand must use 'sudo' — lifecycle hooks run as vscode, not root (see Contract 3 failure modes)"
assert "chown" in oncreate, "onCreateCommand must run chown to fix root-owned mount point"
assert "/home/vscode/.config/gh" in oncreate, "onCreateCommand chown must target the gh config mount path"
assert "vscode:vscode" in oncreate or "vscode " in oncreate, \
    "onCreateCommand chown must set ownership to vscode user"

# containerEnv: no tracked PAT injection (XIX-adjacent; reserved as enterprise override per FR-007)
env = d.get("containerEnv") or {}
for forbidden_key in ("GITHUB_TOKEN", "GH_TOKEN", "GITHUB_PAT"):
    assert forbidden_key not in env, \
        f"{forbidden_key} forbidden in tracked containerEnv (FR-005, FR-007)"

print("OK: Contract 1 static verification passed")
```
