## Contract 3 — Named volumes for `gh` + `entire` auth persistence

Two named volumes, same lifecycle and ownership rules. Each tool's auth state survives container rebuilds via its own volume.

| Property | gh volume | entire volume |
|---|---|---|
| Volume name | `ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config` | `ado-git-repo-insights-entire-config` |
| Mount target | `/home/vscode/.config/gh` | `/home/vscode/.entire` |
| Mount type | `volume` (Docker named volume, NOT bind mount) | `volume` (Docker named volume, NOT bind mount) |
| Mount owner (inside container) | `vscode:vscode` (uid 1000) | `vscode:vscode` (uid 1000) |
| Declared in | `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json::mounts` (tracked) | `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json::mounts` (tracked) |
| Lifecycle | Persists independently of container lifecycle until explicit `docker volume rm` | Persists independently of container lifecycle until explicit `docker volume rm` |
| Chown step (onCreateCommand) | Same single `sudo chown -R vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.config/gh /home/vscode/.entire` invocation covers BOTH | (covered above) |

**Contract:**

- After a contributor runs `gh auth login` once in the container, `gh` writes `hosts.yml`, `oauth_token`, and other config into `/home/vscode/.config/gh/` → the named volume.
- On subsequent container rebuilds, Dev Containers reattaches the same named volume; `gh auth status` reports the persisted authentication without any re-login flow.
- Volume removal (`docker volume rm ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config`) on the host evicts auth; next container creation requires a fresh `gh auth login`.
- The volume is host-local; it does NOT travel with the repo across machines. Per-developer state, per-developer setup.

**Failure modes the contract makes diagnosable:**

| Symptom | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `gh auth status` "not logged in" after rebuild | `mounts` block missing volume entry, OR volume manually removed | Confirm tracked `devcontainer.json::mounts` has the entry; rerun `gh auth login` |
| **`gh auth login` fails with EACCES on first run** | **`onCreateCommand` chown step is missing** — the named volume's mount point landed root-owned by Docker default and the `vscode` user can't write `hosts.yml`. **Empirically reproduced by the D-2 mechanism test (research.md §D-2)**; this is an ACTIVE requirement, not a hypothetical failure mode. | Add `"onCreateCommand": "sudo chown -R vscode:vscode /home/vscode/.config/gh"` to tracked `devcontainer.json` (already in Contract 1). The chown runs ONCE per container creation as `vscode` with passwordless sudo (the Microsoft base image configures this; if a future base-image change removes passwordless sudo, this contract escalates — see below). |
| **`onCreateCommand` itself fails with "sudo: a password is required"** | A future base image change removes the passwordless-sudo configuration for the `vscode` user. | Verify base image with `docker run --rm -u 1000:1000 <image> sudo -n -v` (exit 0 = passwordless sudo works). If broken, fix options in priority order: (a) revert to a base image with passwordless sudo, (b) restructure the chown to a custom entrypoint script via `runArgs`, (c) use `containerUser: root` for the lifecycle hook only. Document the chosen path in the failing PR. |
| Volume present but `gh auth status` says "not logged in" | `hosts.yml` not written (network failure during `gh auth login`, or `gh` config dir resolved elsewhere) | Verify `cat /home/vscode/.config/gh/hosts.yml`; re-run `gh auth login` |

**No token is committed anywhere in this contract**: the volume is host-local; `hosts.yml` lives only in the Docker volume's storage; the image build never sees it.

# drift to match TEST_VOL anywhere in this script.

readonly TEST_VOL="${PROD_VOL}-c4c-test-$(date +%s%N)-$$"

  exit 1
fi

readonly TESTDIR=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dc-c4c-XXXXXXXX")

cleanup() {
  local status=$?
  # Remove the test container by Dev Container CLI's label (no `devcontainer down` subcommand exists).
  docker ps -aq --filter "label=devcontainer.local_folder=$TESTDIR" \
    | xargs -r docker rm -f >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

cfg["mounts"] = rewritten

# Override postCreateCommand to a no-op. We are validating onCreateCommand
# semantics only; repo-dep installs (pnpm install, uv sync, etc.) need the real
# workspace tree and are irrelevant to FR-005 contract verification.
cfg["postCreateCommand"] = "true"

# Do not modify onCreateCommand: the chown targets /home/vscode/.config/gh
# (the mount target), which is unchanged by the volume-name rewrite.
with open(dst_path, "w") as f:
    json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2)
PYEOF

# Bring up the test container; the devcontainer CLI runs onCreateCommand
# (sudo chown) as part of the lifecycle.
devcontainer up --workspace-folder "$TESTDIR" 2>&1 | tail -20

# Verify ownership + writability as vscode, in the freshly-created isolated container.
devcontainer exec --workspace-folder "$TESTDIR" bash -c '
  set -euo pipefail
  echo "--- mount point ownership ---"
  ls -ld /home/vscode/.config/gh
  owner_group=$(stat -c "%U:%G" /home/vscode/.config/gh)
  if [[ "$owner_group" != "vscode:vscode" ]]; then
    echo "FAIL: mount owner is $owner_group, expected vscode:vscode (onCreateCommand sudo chown did not run or failed)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "--- vscode write test ---"
  testfile=/home/vscode/.config/gh/contract-4c-write-probe
  touch "$testfile"
  rm "$testfile"
  echo "OK: FR-005 contract verified on test-isolated volume ('"$TEST_VOL"')"
'
# trap cleanup EXIT removes ONLY the test-scoped volume, the test container, and the temp workspace.
```

Exit 0 = Contract 4c passes (chown ran, vscode can write to a freshly-created test-isolated volume). Exit non-zero = either `onCreateCommand` is missing (Contract 1's static check should have caught this first), the chown is malformed (wrong path, missing `sudo`, base image lost passwordless sudo per Contract 3 escalation row), or the devcontainer CLI failed to execute `onCreateCommand`.

This check is **strictly stronger** than Contract 1's static check — it catches:

- `onCreateCommand` is present in JSON but malformed (chowning the wrong path).
- Passwordless sudo broke in the base image (Contract 3 escalation row).
- Named volume name in `mounts` doesn't match what `onCreateCommand` chowns (typo).
- The devcontainer CLI doesn't actually execute `onCreateCommand` for some configuration reason.

**Why the safety invariants matter**: an earlier draft of Contract 4c used `VOL=ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config-c4c` for `docker volume rm` but invoked `devcontainer up --workspace-folder .` which reads the **production** `devcontainer.json::mounts` (production volume name, no `-c4c` suffix). Result: the test would have mounted the contributor's real auth volume; the chown check could pass on already-correct ownership from a previous login (false positive on stale state); and the cleanup step `rm -f /home/vscode/.config/gh/*` would have wiped the contributor's actual `gh auth login` credentials. The rewritten Contract 4c above isolates the test from production state at every step (test-scoped volume name, temp workspace with rewritten config, pre-existence assertion, `trap` cleanup, explicit name guard before rm) so neither failure mode is reachable.

Run Contract 4c on every PR that touches `.devcontainer/`, plus once in the CI verification job for the implementation PR (logged alongside FR-013/SC-005).

# Quickstart — Dev Container Refactor

This is the contributor-facing first-run guide for the refactored dev container. It assumes the implementation PR has landed and the new image (`ghcr.io/oddessentials/ado-git-repo-insights-dev:main`) has been republished by the `publish-devcontainer` CI job.

The two auth surfaces — **git HTTPS credentials** and **GitHub CLI credentials** — are independent. Verify them separately. A working `git push` does NOT imply a working `gh`, and vice versa.

---

## Prerequisites (one-time, host-side)

- Docker runtime: Docker Desktop ≥4.32, OrbStack ≥1.7, or Rancher Desktop ≥1.13.
- VS Code with the Dev Containers extension installed AND the GitHub authentication provider signed in (Sign in via the Accounts gear → GitHub).
- Repository cloned to a path with no spaces or unusual characters.

---

## First-run (5 minutes, once per machine)

### 1. Open in container

```text
VS Code → Command Palette (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P) → "Dev Containers: Reopen in Container"
```

Wait for `postCreateCommand` to complete (one-time dependency install: ~3–5 min on warm cache; ~10–15 min on cold cache with Playwright Chromium download).

### 2. Verify the image (image-only check; no auth required)

```bash
# Inside the container's integrated terminal:
node --version       # expected: 22.x.x
pnpm --version       # expected: 9.15.0
python --version     # expected: 3.12.x
uv --version         # expected: 0.11.9
gh --version         # expected: matches GH_VERSION pinned in Dockerfile
specify --version    # expected: 0.9.2
gitleaks version     # expected: 8.18.4
```

All eight commands MUST succeed. If any fails, the image is broken — file an issue; do NOT proceed with the auth setup steps below.

### 3. Authenticate `gh` (one-time; persists via named volume)

```bash
gh auth status
# Expected: "You are not logged into any GitHub hosts. Run gh auth login to authenticate."
# This is the documented baseline — NOT an error. Proceed to login.

gh auth login
# Follow the interactive prompts:
#   - GitHub.com (not GitHub Enterprise unless your org requires)
#   - HTTPS (recommended; SSH option also works if you've configured Contract 3 SSH override)
#   - Authenticate via web browser (recommended) OR paste a personal access token
#   - The browser flow opens a tab; complete the device-code prompt
# After the flow completes:

gh auth status
# Expected: "Logged in to github.com account <your-github-username>
#            Active account: true
#            Git operations protocol: https
#            Token: gho_*****"
```

Your auth state is now persisted in the Docker named volume `ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config`. It survives container rebuilds.

### 3a. Authenticate `entire` (one-time; optional but recommended)

```bash
entire --version
# Expected: entire 0.7.3 (or pinned version per Version Inventory)

entire login
# Follow the device-flow prompts (browser opens for entire.io auth).
# After login:

entire auth status      # or `entire activity` to confirm session capture is active
# Expected: authenticated as your entire.io account.
```

Your entire auth state is persisted in the named volume `ado-git-repo-insights-entire-config` and survives rebuilds. `entire`'s git hooks are wired into `postCreateCommand` (see FR-020) — once you've logged in, your AI agent sessions (claude code, codex) are indexed against your commits on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch IN this repo. Telemetry is disabled at the repo level via tracked `.entire/settings.json`.

**If you don't want session capture**: skip `entire login`. The binary is installed and the hooks fire, but they no-op without an active session. All commits, pushes, and PR creation work unchanged.

### 4. Verify git HTTPS (independent auth surface)

```bash
git config --get credential.helper
# Expected: a long line beginning with "!f() { ... vscode-server ... git-credential-helper $*; }; f"
# This is VS Code's injected credential-helper proxy.

git push --dry-run
# Expected: success without credential prompt.
# If it prompts, your host VS Code is not signed into GitHub — sign in via Accounts gear, then retry.
```

---

## Routine verification (after any container rebuild)

```bash
# Verify gh auth persisted across rebuild
gh auth status
# Expected: still "Logged in to github.com account <user>"

# Verify a real round-trip
gh api user --jq .login
# Expected: prints your GitHub username

gh pr create --fill --draft --dry-run
# Expected: prints the would-be PR body without erroring on auth
# (Run against a real PR-eligible branch — current branch must have a base it can target.)

# Verify git HTTPS still independent and working
git push --dry-run
# Expected: success without prompt
```

If `gh auth status` says "not logged in" after a rebuild but the named volume exists (`docker volume ls | grep ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config`), the mount is misconfigured — check `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json::mounts` for the correct volume entry.

---

## Recovery scenarios

### Re-authenticate `gh` (forgotten which account, switched accounts, token expired)

```bash
gh auth logout
gh auth login   # repeat the flow from step 3 above
```

### Reset the named volume completely (clean slate)

```bash
# Host-side:
docker volume rm ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config
# Then in VS Code: Dev Containers: Rebuild Container
# Then in the container: gh auth login (from step 3)
```

### Host VS Code signed out of GitHub mid-session

```bash
# Inside the container:
git push --dry-run
# Prompts for credentials (host helper can't broker without VS Code session)
```

Fix on the host: VS Code → Accounts gear → Sign in to GitHub. Then in the container, retry `git push --dry-run`. (`gh` is unaffected — it uses its own named-volume auth.)

### Switch to SSH-based git (uncommitted local override, FR-007)

Add the following to your **uncommitted local edit** of `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` (do NOT commit):

```jsonc
{
  // ... existing tracked content ...
  "mounts": [
    "source=ado-git-repo-insights-gh-config,target=/home/vscode/.config/gh,type=volume",
    // Uncommitted local addition:
    "source=${env:SSH_AUTH_SOCK},target=/ssh-agent,type=bind,readonly"
  ],
  "containerEnv": {
    "SSH_AUTH_SOCK": "/ssh-agent"
  }
}
```

Verify after rebuild:

```bash
ssh-add -l                     # expected: lists your host's keys
ssh -T git@github.com          # expected: "Hi <user>! You've successfully authenticated"
```

---

## When to file an issue vs. handle locally

| Symptom | Likely cause | First step |
|---|---|---|
| Step 2 (image verify) fails | Image build defect; CI republish broken | File an issue with the failing tool name + version output |
| Step 3 `gh auth login` succeeds but `gh auth status` still says "not logged in" | Local browser flow incomplete; `hosts.yml` not written | Retry `gh auth login` |
| Step 4 `git push --dry-run` prompts | Host VS Code signed out of GitHub | Sign in on the host; retry |
| Routine verification — auth lost after rebuild | Named volume removed OR `mounts` entry broken | Inspect `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` and `docker volume ls` |
| Routine verification — `gh pr create --dry-run` fails with "no base branch" | Local branch has no upstream OR no PR-eligible base | Push the branch first; create a base branch reference |

---

## What's NOT in the image (intentional)

- **Claude Code, Codex, or any other personal AI assistant CLI.** These are developer-personal tooling per `.gitignore` (excludes `.codex`, `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`) and are intentionally not installed by the image or `postCreateCommand`. Install via dotfiles repo or optional named-volume + uncommitted local mount.
- **SSH agent forwarding** (default). Available as uncommitted local override per the SSH scenario above and FR-007.
- **GPG agent / commit signing** (default). Available as uncommitted local override per FR-007.
- **`containerEnv` PAT injection** (default). Available only as a documented enterprise override with stakeholder approval (FR-007). The named-volume `gh auth login` model is the documented default.

---

## Where things live (for the curious)

- `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` — pinned system layer (gitleaks SHA-verified, Playwright apt deps, unzip, uv, **`gh` via `cli.github.com` apt**, **Spec Kit via uv tool + git commit pin**).
- `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` — pinned Node Feature, named-volume mount.
- `.devcontainer/README.md` — full failure-UX flowcharts, four-scenario guide (FR-017).
- `LOCAL_CI_PARITY_INVARIANTS.md` — gate-by-gate parity contract; the refactor preserves it.
- `specs/364-devcontainer-refactor/` — this spec's documentation (locally; `specs/` is gitignored per docs/specs-retirement.md).

1	# Local/CI Parity Invariants
2	
3	This document is the authoritative reference for CI/local check parity in ado-git-repo-insights. Every CI quality gate has a verified local equivalent that runs automatically via git hooks, ensuring developers cannot push code that fails CI. The local PR preflight is authoritative by default and fails closed if a CI-hard gate cannot run.
4	
5	This document records **invariants and contracts**, not point-in-time state. It does not track drift-prone numbers (test counts, historical failure tallies, line offsets, `Last verified` dates, or gate counts). Authoritative values live in the source files the document references — [scripts/run_pr_preflight.py](scripts/run_pr_preflight.py), [scripts/run_repo_hook.py](scripts/run_repo_hook.py), [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml), [.pre-commit-config.yaml](.pre-commit-config.yaml), and the hook scripts under [.husky/](.husky/). If a number would need manual updating to stay truthful, it belongs in code, not here.
6	
7	## How It Works
8	
9	```
10	git commit  -->  .husky/pre-commit  -->  run_repo_hook.py pre-commit  -->  Tier 1 checks
11	git push    -->  .husky/pre-push    -->  run_repo_hook.py pre-push    -->  Tier 2 checks (includes full preflight)
12	```
13	
14	The Tier 1 / Tier 2 labels describe *when* a given run fires, not strict hook
15	exclusivity. A handful of framework-provided hooks in
16	`.pre-commit-config.yaml` register for both stages (e.g. `detect-private-key`,
17	`check-added-large-files`, `check-merge-conflict`, `env-guard`,
18	`tool-version-parity`) and therefore fire on both commit and push — the YAML
19	is authoritative for the current set.
20	
21	**Only bypass**: `--no-verify` flag, which is forbidden by project policy.
22

40	## Commit Message Gate (automatic on `git commit`)
41	
42	| #   | CI Check   | Local Equivalent              | Parity   | Prevention Proof                                                                            | How It Can Never Happen Again                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
43	| --- | ---------- | ----------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
44	| 7f  | commitlint | `pnpm exec commitlint --edit` | Weaker\* | [.husky/commit-msg](.husky/commit-msg), [ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml) `commitlint` job | **CI is authoritative.** CI validates all PR commits via `commitlint --from origin/main --to HEAD`. Locally, the `.husky/commit-msg` hook runs `pnpm exec commitlint --edit` — but see Known Inconsistency below. Config: [commitlint.config.cjs](commitlint.config.cjs) extends `@commitlint/config-conventional` with `ratchet` added to `type-enum` for internal ratchet floor-bump commits, ignores merge commits. Semantic-release commits use `HUSKY=0` in CI to bypass hooks — the release commit format (`chore(release): X.Y.Z [skip ci]`) passes commitlint regardless. Pytest guard: [test_hook_guards.py](tests/unit/test_hook_guards.py) `TestCommitlintInfrastructure`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
45	
46	**Known Inconsistency (Weaker\*):** The local commit-msg hook depends on husky's internal dispatcher (`.husky/_/commit-msg`) being intact. External tools that manage git hooks (e.g. `entire`) can overwrite this dispatcher, silently breaking the chain to commitlint. A pre-commit health check warns when this is detected and prints the fix command (`pnpm exec husky`), but does **not** block — because the external tool re-injects on every commit, creating an unwinnable loop if the check were fatal. **CI is the authoritative gate.** Malformed commit messages will always be caught on PR, even if the local hook is bypassed. This is an accepted asymmetry: local enforcement is best-effort developer UX; CI enforcement is mandatory.

127	## Known Tradeoffs (Documented, Accepted)
128	
129	| Tradeoff                                                     | Rationale                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
130	| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
131	| Python tests run on baseline Python only (not 3×3 matrix)    | Full matrix is slow; baseline catches the majority of issues. Cross-platform bugs (Windows paths, macOS timing) are CI-discovered.                                                                                                   |
132	| Python build is sdist-only (CI also builds wheel)            | sdist catches the majority of packaging issues. Wheel-only failures have not been observed in practice.                                                                                                                              |

# Local/CI Parity Invariants

This document is the authoritative reference for CI/local check parity in ado-git-repo-insights. Every CI quality gate has a verified local equivalent that runs automatically via git hooks, ensuring developers cannot push code that fails CI. The local PR preflight is authoritative by default and fails closed if a CI-hard gate cannot run.

This document records **invariants and contracts**, not point-in-time state. It does not track drift-prone numbers (test counts, historical failure tallies, line offsets, `Last verified` dates, or gate counts). Authoritative values live in the source files the document references — [scripts/run_pr_preflight.py](scripts/run_pr_preflight.py), [scripts/run_repo_hook.py](scripts/run_repo_hook.py), [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml), [.pre-commit-config.yaml](.pre-commit-config.yaml), and the hook scripts under [.husky/](.husky/). If a number would need manual updating to stay truthful, it belongs in code, not here.

## How It Works

```
git commit  -->  .husky/pre-commit  -->  run_repo_hook.py pre-commit  -->  Tier 1 checks
git push    -->  .husky/pre-push    -->  run_repo_hook.py pre-push    -->  Tier 2 checks (includes full preflight)
```

The Tier 1 / Tier 2 labels describe *when* a given run fires, not strict hook
exclusivity. A handful of framework-provided hooks in
`.pre-commit-config.yaml` register for both stages (e.g. `detect-private-key`,
`check-added-large-files`, `check-merge-conflict`, `env-guard`,
`tool-version-parity`) and therefore fire on both commit and push — the YAML
is authoritative for the current set.

**Only bypass**: `--no-verify` flag, which is forbidden by project policy.

## Commit Message Gate (automatic on `git commit`)

| #   | CI Check   | Local Equivalent              | Parity   | Prevention Proof                                                                            | How It Can Never Happen Again                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --- | ---------- | ----------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 7f  | commitlint | `pnpm exec commitlint --edit` | Weaker\* | [.husky/commit-msg](.husky/commit-msg), [ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml) `commitlint` job | **CI is authoritative.** CI validates all PR commits via `commitlint --from origin/main --to HEAD`. Locally, the `.husky/commit-msg` hook runs `pnpm exec commitlint --edit` — but see Known Inconsistency below. Config: [commitlint.config.cjs](commitlint.config.cjs) extends `@commitlint/config-conventional` with `ratchet` added to `type-enum` for internal ratchet floor-bump commits, ignores merge commits. Semantic-release commits use `HUSKY=0` in CI to bypass hooks — the release commit format (`chore(release): X.Y.Z [skip ci]`) passes commitlint regardless. Pytest guard: [test_hook_guards.py](tests/unit/test_hook_guards.py) `TestCommitlintInfrastructure`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

**Known Inconsistency (Weaker\*):** The local commit-msg hook depends on husky's internal dispatcher (`.husky/_/commit-msg`) being intact. External tools that manage git hooks (e.g. `entire`) can overwrite this dispatcher, silently breaking the chain to commitlint. A pre-commit health check warns when this is detected and prints the fix command (`pnpm exec husky`), but does **not** block — because the external tool re-injects on every commit, creating an unwinnable loop if the check were fatal. **CI is the authoritative gate.** Malformed commit messages will always be caught on PR, even if the local hook is bypassed. This is an accepted asymmetry: local enforcement is best-effort developer UX; CI enforcement is mandatory.

## Known Tradeoffs (Documented, Accepted)

| Tradeoff                                                     | Rationale                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Python tests run on baseline Python only (not 3×3 matrix)    | Full matrix is slow; baseline catches the majority of issues. Cross-platform bugs (Windows paths, macOS timing) are CI-discovered.                                                                                                   |
| Python build is sdist-only (CI also builds wheel)            | sdist catches the majority of packaging issues. Wheel-only failures have not been observed in practice.                                                                                                                              |
| Scalability tests are CI-only                                | Synthetic data generation is expensive; run on demand locally via `pnpm run test:scalability`.                                                                                                                                       |
| Fresh-clone-verify is CI-only                                | Cannot simulate fresh clone without re-cloning. Verifies lockfile determinism.                                                                                                                                                       |
| mypy is Tier 2 (pre-push), not Tier 1 (pre-commit)           | Requires `[ml]` optional deps for full coverage; not every commit-stage environment has them. Pre-push catches errors before code leaves the machine. Parity is Match at Tier 2.                                                     |

If a gate compiles files from multiple directories (e.g., `tsconfig.test.json` includes `tests/`, `ui/`, and `types/`), the trigger must fire for changes to any of those directories. Define triggers by what the compiler reads, not by what the developer intends to change. If a tsconfig gains a new include path, add a trigger and a regression test. Regression tests: [tests/unit/test_hook_triggers.py](tests/unit/test_hook_triggers.py).
141	- **Weakening a local check**: MUST document rationale in this file. CI-hard-gate checks must never exist in a weaker local mode. `python scripts/run_pr_preflight.py --allow-local-degraded` is diagnostic-only and never counts as parity.
142	- **Pre-commit selectivity (Tier 1 asymmetry)**: Pre-commit gates are intentionally selective — they run only when relevant files are staged, not unconditionally. This is a performance tradeoff: pre-push (Tier 2) runs unconditionally and catches anything pre-commit missed. The asymmetry is between Tier 1 and Tier 2, not between local and CI. This is by design, not a defect.
143	- **Clean-worktree guards**: Any pre-commit gate that reads the worktree (tsc, parity script, etc.) MUST have a corresponding clean-worktree guard covering its full input scope. The guard blocks commit if unstaged changes exist in any path the gate reads. Current guards: `require_clean_ui_sources()` (extension/ui/), `require_clean_test_compilation_scope()` (extension/tests/, extension/ui/, types/), `require_clean_tsconfigs()` (extension/tsconfig*.json).
144	- **Entry point alignment**: When adding a new gate to CI or pre-commit, also add it to `pnpm test:ci` in the root `package.json`. The root `test:ci` script is the documented local equivalent of the CI gate chain — if they diverge, `pnpm test:ci` can pass while CI fails. The `test:ci` script runs the suppression audit first, then all CI gates (ruff, mypy, pytest, tsc, eslint, jest, smoke).
145	- **Verify before commit**: Every new gate, guard, trigger, pathspec, or config change MUST be mechanically verified against real execution before committing. If you cannot point to terminal output proving the change works, do not commit it. Verify the success path AND the failure path.
146	- **Test count ratcheting**: The authoritative floor lives in [.test-floor-contract.json](.test-floor-contract.json). Both [run_pr_preflight.py](scripts/run_pr_preflight.py) and [ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml) read it via `--min-collected-artifact`; no hardcoded integer exists in either file. The Python floor MUST use the **cross-platform minimum** collected count — see "Platform-Conditional Test Collection" below. Cross-OS equality of the Python floor is enforced by the `python-collection-parity` CI job which compares exact node_id sets between Ubuntu and Windows. The Extension floor uses the exact actual count (single CI environment, no matrix). Zero-tolerance on discovery count; `--max-skips` handles execution variance separately. When adding tests, bump `.test-floor-contract.json` by exactly the delta in the same commit. When removing tests, update with PR justification. Per-commit enforcement is done by **Tier 2 Row 27a** (`check_ratchet_bump.py`), which walks the first-parent range and compares per-commit `floor_delta` vs `actual_delta`. Bypass: `[ratchet-realignment]` or `[ratchet-test-removal]` in the **subject line of the specific commit** that introduced the delta (scanned via `git log --oneline`; markers in bodies are NOT honored; markers on other commits in the range do NOT cover unrelated commits). **Collection-time stability rule**: shared-floor Python tests must be defined unconditionally across the canonical interpreter lane. Python-version branching may change execution (for example, `pytest.skip(...)` inside the test body) but must not hide or create `def test_*` definitions at import time, or the collected floor will drift by interpreter version.
147	- **`--no-verify`**: Forbidden by project policy. Never bypass git hooks.
148	- **Reviewing this document**: After any CI pipeline change, verify parity by running the full preflight locally: `python scripts/run_pr_preflight.py`.
149	- **Split tsconfig architecture**: The extension uses separate configs for type checking (`tsconfig.json`: `module: "ES2022"`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`) and build emission (`tsconfig.build.json`: `module: "CommonJS"`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`). The `build:tsc` script in `package.json` MUST reference `tsconfig.build.json` explicitly. **`dist/ui/` is owned exclusively by esbuild (`build:ui`)**; `tsconfig.build.json` MUST NOT include `ui/` — otherwise `build:tsc` silently overwrites IIFE bundles with CJS, breaking browser runtime. Guard: [build-output-format-guard.test.ts](extension/tests/meta/build-output-format-guard.test.ts) pins module + moduleResolution for each config, the build script entry point, and ui/ exclusion from build scope. When upgrading TypeScript, verify both configs resolve to their expected values.
150	
151	## Platform-Conditional Test Collection
152	
153	Python CI runs the OS × Python matrix declared in [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml). Some tests are platform-specific (e.g., Windows console handler tests). These must **never** use `pytest.mark.skip`, `pytest.mark.skipIf`, or runtime `pytest.skip()` calls because CI enforces `--max-skips=0`. Any form of skip — declarative or runtime — counts against the zero-tolerance gate.
154	
155	**Pattern**: Platform-conditional tests live in files named `test_*_windows.py` (or `_linux.py`, `_macos.py` when added). The glob patterns that match those files are declared once in [scripts/_platform_test_filters.py](scripts/_platform_test_filters.py) as `PLATFORM_CONDITIONAL_IGNORE_GLOBS` and imported by both [tests/conftest.py](tests/conftest.py) (`collect_ignore_glob` on non-Windows) and [scripts/check_ratchet_bump.py](scripts/check_ratchet_bump.py) (`--ignore-glob` CLI flags for its hermetic subprocess). A parity test in [tests/unit/test_platform_conditional_collection.py](tests/unit/test_platform_conditional_collection.py) asserts at the AST level that **both** call sites import the shared constant — either side dropping the import fails the test immediately, so the filter sets cannot drift.
156	
157	This means:
158	
159	- On Windows: all tests are collected (including `test_*_windows.py`)
160	- On Linux/macOS: files matching `PLATFORM_CONDITIONAL_IGNORE_GLOBS` are never discovered — they don't count as collected or skipped
161	- The `--min-collected` threshold MUST use the **cross-platform minimum** — the count pytest produces when the shared globs are applied. This is what Linux/macOS cells see and what Windows cells see after the filter is applied.
162	
163	**Cross-platform minimum vs. Windows hermetic full count**: On a Windows machine, a hermetic `pytest --collect-only` without the platform-conditional `--ignore-glob` filter reports a number **larger** than the floor because it sees the platform-conditional files. The ratchet-bump gate prints both numbers — the floor-comparison number is labeled `cross-platform (Windows-filtered)` and the un-filtered number is labeled `Windows hermetic full count (no platform filter)` — so the Windows-machine developer can reconcile the two. Both numbers come from the same hermetic code path (plugins disabled, `PYTEST_ADDOPTS`/`PYTEST_PLUGINS` scrubbed, `-o addopts=` cleared); the Windows hermetic full count is NOT what a bare `pytest --collect-only` in an arbitrarily-configured developer shell would return — it is what Windows CI cells see, which is the relevant comparison point for ratchet-bump drift. The delta between the two numbers is derived at runtime from `scripts._platform_test_filters.count_platform_conditional_test_functions`, which AST-walks every file matched by `PLATFORM_CONDITIONAL_IGNORE_GLOBS` — never hardcoded, and extensible to Linux/macOS conventions without any helper edit. 164	
165	**Adding new platform-conditional tests**:
166	
167	1. Create a file whose name matches one of the patterns in `PLATFORM_CONDITIONAL_IGNORE_GLOBS` (currently `test_*_windows.py`). If you are adding a Linux- or macOS-only test, extend `PLATFORM_CONDITIONAL_IGNORE_GLOBS` with the new pattern — both conftest and the gate pick it up automatically.
168	2. Do NOT use `pytest.mark.skip` — use the collection exclusion pattern.
169	3. Re-measure the cross-platform minimum. The authoritative method is to run the ratchet-bump guard: `python scripts/check_ratchet_bump.py --base-ref origin/main --junit-extension extension/test-results.xml`. Its output line `actual=N (cross-platform (Windows-filtered))` is the correct floor regardless of the developer's OS. (Bare `pytest --collect-only` on a Windows machine over-reports by the platform delta.)
170	4. Update `python.min_collected` in [.test-floor-contract.json](.test-floor-contract.json) to the reported number in the same commit. Both [run_pr_preflight.py](scripts/run_pr_preflight.py) and [ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml) read from this artifact — no other file needs editing. Cross-OS parity of the new floor is proven by the `python-collection-parity` CI job on each PR.
171	
172	**Interpreter-version parity rule**: the shared Python floor is measured on the canonical Python lane (`3.12` in CI today), but collection must stay stable across supported interpreters for any test that contributes to that floor. Do not wrap `def test_*` definitions in module- or class-level `if _IS_BASELINE_PYTHON:` branches. If a behavior is baseline-only, define the test unconditionally and call `pytest.skip(...)` inside the body on non-baseline interpreters. That keeps collection stable while preserving runtime semantics.

186	# ado-git-repo-insights Constitution
187	
188	This constitution codifies the non-negotiable governance principles for ado-git-repo-insights.
189	All implementation choices, code changes, and architectural decisions MUST preserve these properties.
190	If a principle cannot be satisfied, the change MUST be escalated as a design break.
191	
192	## Core Principles (Immutable)
193	
194	The following 26 principles are immutable. Any modification requires a MAJOR version bump
195	and explicit migration plan with stakeholder approval.
196	
197	### I. CSV Schema Contract
198	
199	CSV schema is a hard contract. Each CSV MUST have exactly the expected columns, in exactly
200	the expected order, with stable names. The CSVs (`organizations`, `projects`, `repositories`,
201	`pull_requests`, `users`, `reviewers`) define the PowerBI integration boundary.
202	
203	### II. No Breaking CSV Changes
204	
205	No breaking changes to CSVs without an explicit version bump and migration plan.
206	Adding, removing, renaming, or reordering columns is a breaking change unless the
207	downstream contract is updated intentionally with documented migration steps.
208	
209	### III. Deterministic CSV Output
210	
211	CSV output MUST be deterministic. For the same SQLite contents, CSV bytes MUST be stable
212	across runs:
213	- Deterministic row ordering (stable sort keys)
214	- Deterministic null/empty-string handling
215	- Stable formatting for datetimes and numbers
216	
217	### IV. PowerBI Frictionless Import
218	
219	PowerBI imports MUST remain frictionless. The CSVs MUST remain loadable into the existing
220	PowerBI model without manual fixes. Any schema drift that breaks import is a blocking defect.
221	
222	### V. SQLite as Source of Truth
223	
224	SQLite is the source of truth for derived outputs. CSVs are generated from SQLite,
225	not from raw API JSON directly. All transformations flow through the database layer.
226	
227	### VI. Pipeline Artifacts as Persistence
228	
229	Pipeline Artifacts are the primary persistence mechanism. The standard run downloads
230	the prior SQLite artifact, updates it, and re-uploads it. This enables incremental
231	extraction without external storage dependencies.
232	
233	### VII. No Publish on Failure
234	
235	If extraction or CSV generation fails, the pipeline MUST NOT publish a mutated SQLite
236	artifact or partial CSV set. The previous good state MUST be preserved.
237	
238	### VIII. Idempotent State Updates
239	
240	State updates MUST be idempotent and converge. Re-running the same date range MUST NOT
241	create duplicate logical entities; it MUST converge via stable keys and UPSERT semantics.
242	
243	### IX. Recoverable Persistence
244	
245	Persistence MUST be recoverable. If the SQLite artifact is missing or expired:
246	- The system MUST initialize a fresh DB
247	- The run MUST be explicit about "first-run/backfill" behavior
248	- The resulting outputs MUST still satisfy the CSV contract
249	
250	### X. Daily Incremental Extraction Default
251	
252	Daily incremental extraction is the default mode. Standard scheduled runs MUST extract
253	the minimal incremental range to optimize API usage and pipeline duration.
254	
255	### XI. Periodic Backfill Required
256	
257	The system MUST support a bounded "backfill window" mode (e.g., weekly) that re-fetches
258	and UPSERTs the last N days (e.g., 30-90). This is the primary mechanism to handle late
259	PR changes without complex change detection.
260	
261	### XII. No Silent Data Loss
262	
263	Pagination MUST be complete (continuation tokens) and failures MUST fail the run rather
264	than produce incomplete "successful" outputs. Silent data loss is a critical defect.
265	
266	### XIII. Bounded Rate Limiting
267	
268	Retries, sleeps, and backoff MUST be bounded and configurable. The system MUST NEVER
269	enter infinite retry loops. Rate limiting failures surface as run failures with
270	actionable diagnostics.
271	
272	### XIV. Stable UPSERT Keys
273	
274	Stable identifiers are required for UPSERT keys. Primary keys MUST be stable across runs
275	(e.g., `repository_id` + `pull_request_id` → `pull_request_uid`).
276	
277	### XV. Organization/Project Scoping
278	
279	All entities MUST be scoped to organization and project where applicable. No table row
280	or CSV row may be ambiguous across org/project boundaries.
281	
282	### XVI. Names as Labels, IDs as Identity
283	
284	Names are labels; IDs are identity. The system MUST support name changes without breaking
285	identity or duplicating entities. Display names are mutable; identifiers are not.
286	
287	### XVII. Cross-Agent Compatibility
288	
289	The Azure DevOps Pipeline Task MUST run in both hosted and self-hosted agents. Any runtime
290	assumptions (Python version, install method, working directory) MUST be explicit and tested.
291	
292	### XVIII. Actionable Failure Logs
293	
294	If configuration is invalid, auth fails, or runtime dependencies are missing, the task
295	MUST fail fast with a direct error message. Logs MUST be actionable for operators.
296	
297	### XIX. PAT Secrecy
298	
299	PATs are secrets and MUST NEVER be logged. Authorization headers and token values MUST
300	be scrubbed from all debug output, including stack traces.
301	
302	### XX. Least Privilege Default
303	
304	PAT requirements MUST be documented and limited to what's necessary (Code Read scope).
305	The system MUST NOT request or require elevated permissions beyond minimum needs.
306	
307	### XXI. Single-Authority Storage Backend
308	
309	Azure Storage fallback is opt-in and MUST be single-authority. When enabled, Azure Storage
310	becomes the persistence source of truth for SQLite. Mixed-mode (artifact + blob both
311	writing state) is forbidden.
312	
313	### XXII. Explicit One-Way Migration
314	
315	If switching to Azure Storage, the plan MUST define a controlled cutover that prevents
316	split-brain state. Migration is explicit and one-way with documented rollback procedures.
317	
318	### XXIII. Automated CSV Contract Validation
319	
320	CI MUST verify CSV schemas and column order against expected definitions. Contract tests
321	run on every PR and block merge on failure.
322	
323	### XXIV. End-to-End Testability
324	
325	At least one integration test MUST validate:
326	- Mocked ADO API responses
327	- SQLite UPSERT convergence
328	- CSV deterministic output
329	
330	The extraction → SQLite → CSV pipeline is testable without live API access.
331	
332	### XXV. Backfill Mode Testing
333	
334	There MUST be a test proving that a late change (e.g., reviewer vote update) is corrected
335	after a backfill run. Backfill convergence is a verified capability.
336	
337	### XXVI. Collection-Stable Test Definitions
338	
339	Shared-floor tests MUST have collection-stable definitions across all supported interpreter
340	and OS lanes. Any Python test that contributes to a ratcheted `--min-collected` floor MUST
341	be defined unconditionally at module scope:
342	- No `if version_condition:` wrappers around `def test_*`
343	- No decorators that add or remove test definitions based on environment
344	- No module-level or class-level import-time gating of test definitions
345	
346	Environment-specific behavior MUST be handled inside the test body (e.g.,
347	`pytest.skip(...)` on non-baseline interpreters), because import-time gating breaks
348	collection parity between local and CI and causes the shared floor to drift by
349	interpreter version or OS lane. Platform-conditional files MUST use the file-name-pattern
350	exclusion mechanism (`test_*_windows.py`, etc.) with the shared
351	`PLATFORM_CONDITIONAL_IGNORE_GLOBS` constant — never `pytest.mark.skip` or runtime
352	`pytest.skip()` at collection time, because `--max-skips=0` treats both as violations.
353

# ado-git-repo-insights Constitution

This constitution codifies the non-negotiable governance principles for ado-git-repo-insights.
All implementation choices, code changes, and architectural decisions MUST preserve these properties.
If a principle cannot be satisfied, the change MUST be escalated as a design break.

## Core Principles (Immutable)

The following 26 principles are immutable. Any modification requires a MAJOR version bump
and explicit migration plan with stakeholder approval.

### I. CSV Schema Contract

CSV schema is a hard contract. Each CSV MUST have exactly the expected columns, in exactly
the expected order, with stable names. The CSVs (`organizations`, `projects`, `repositories`,
`pull_requests`, `users`, `reviewers`) define the PowerBI integration boundary.

### II. No Breaking CSV Changes

No breaking changes to CSVs without an explicit version bump and migration plan.
Adding, removing, renaming, or reordering columns is a breaking change unless the
downstream contract is updated intentionally with documented migration steps.

### III. Deterministic CSV Output

CSV output MUST be deterministic. For the same SQLite contents, CSV bytes MUST be stable
across runs:
- Deterministic row ordering (stable sort keys)
- Deterministic null/empty-string handling
- Stable formatting for datetimes and numbers

### IV. PowerBI Frictionless Import

PowerBI imports MUST remain frictionless. The CSVs MUST remain loadable into the existing
PowerBI model without manual fixes. Any schema drift that breaks import is a blocking defect.

### V. SQLite as Source of Truth

SQLite is the source of truth for derived outputs. CSVs are generated from SQLite,
not from raw API JSON directly. All transformations flow through the database layer.

### VI. Pipeline Artifacts as Persistence

Pipeline Artifacts are the primary persistence mechanism. The standard run downloads
the prior SQLite artifact, updates it, and re-uploads it. This enables incremental
extraction without external storage dependencies.

### VII. No Publish on Failure

If extraction or CSV generation fails, the pipeline MUST NOT publish a mutated SQLite
artifact or partial CSV set. The previous good state MUST be preserved.

### VIII. Idempotent State Updates

State updates MUST be idempotent and converge. Re-running the same date range MUST NOT
create duplicate logical entities; it MUST converge via stable keys and UPSERT semantics.

### IX. Recoverable Persistence

Persistence MUST be recoverable. If the SQLite artifact is missing or expired:
- The system MUST initialize a fresh DB
- The run MUST be explicit about "first-run/backfill" behavior
- The resulting outputs MUST still satisfy the CSV contract

### X. Daily Incremental Extraction Default

Daily incremental extraction is the default mode. Standard scheduled runs MUST extract
the minimal incremental range to optimize API usage and pipeline duration.

### XI. Periodic Backfill Required

The system MUST support a bounded "backfill window" mode (e.g., weekly) that re-fetches
and UPSERTs the last N days (e.g., 30-90). This is the primary mechanism to handle late
PR changes without complex change detection.

### XII. No Silent Data Loss

Pagination MUST be complete (continuation tokens) and failures MUST fail the run rather
than produce incomplete "successful" outputs. Silent data loss is a critical defect.

### XIII. Bounded Rate Limiting

Retries, sleeps, and backoff MUST be bounded and configurable. The system MUST NEVER
enter infinite retry loops. Rate limiting failures surface as run failures with
actionable diagnostics.

### XIV. Stable UPSERT Keys

Stable identifiers are required for UPSERT keys. Primary keys MUST be stable across runs
(e.g., `repository_id` + `pull_request_id` → `pull_request_uid`).

### XV. Organization/Project Scoping

All entities MUST be scoped to organization and project where applicable. No table row
or CSV row may be ambiguous across org/project boundaries.

### XVI. Names as Labels, IDs as Identity

Names are labels; IDs are identity. The system MUST support name changes without breaking
identity or duplicating entities. Display names are mutable; identifiers are not.

### XVII. Cross-Agent Compatibility

The Azure DevOps Pipeline Task MUST run in both hosted and self-hosted agents. Any runtime
assumptions (Python version, install method, working directory) MUST be explicit and tested.

### XVIII. Actionable Failure Logs

If configuration is invalid, auth fails, or runtime dependencies are missing, the task
MUST fail fast with a direct error message. Logs MUST be actionable for operators.

### XIX. PAT Secrecy

PATs are secrets and MUST NEVER be logged. Authorization headers and token values MUST
be scrubbed from all debug output, including stack traces.

### XX. Least Privilege Default

PAT requirements MUST be documented and limited to what's necessary (Code Read scope).
The system MUST NOT request or require elevated permissions beyond minimum needs.

### XXI. Single-Authority Storage Backend

Azure Storage fallback is opt-in and MUST be single-authority. When enabled, Azure Storage
becomes the persistence source of truth for SQLite. Mixed-mode (artifact + blob both
writing state) is forbidden.

### XXII. Explicit One-Way Migration

If switching to Azure Storage, the plan MUST define a controlled cutover that prevents
split-brain state. Migration is explicit and one-way with documented rollback procedures.

### XXIII. Automated CSV Contract Validation

CI MUST verify CSV schemas and column order against expected definitions. Contract tests
run on every PR and block merge on failure.

### XXIV. End-to-End Testability

At least one integration test MUST validate:
- Mocked ADO API responses
- SQLite UPSERT convergence
- CSV deterministic output

The extraction → SQLite → CSV pipeline is testable without live API access.

### XXV. Backfill Mode Testing

There MUST be a test proving that a late change (e.g., reviewer vote update) is corrected
after a backfill run. Backfill convergence is a verified capability.

### XXVI. Collection-Stable Test Definitions

Shared-floor tests MUST have collection-stable definitions across all supported interpreter
and OS lanes. Any Python test that contributes to a ratcheted `--min-collected` floor MUST
be defined unconditionally at module scope:
- No `if version_condition:` wrappers around `def test_*`
- No decorators that add or remove test definitions based on environment
- No module-level or class-level import-time gating of test definitions

Environment-specific behavior MUST be handled inside the test body (e.g.,
`pytest.skip(...)` on non-baseline interpreters), because import-time gating breaks
collection parity between local and CI and causes the shared floor to drift by
interpreter version or OS lane. Platform-conditional files MUST use the file-name-pattern
exclusion mechanism (`test_*_windows.py`, etc.) with the shared
`PLATFORM_CONDITIONAL_IGNORE_GLOBS` constant — never `pytest.mark.skip` or runtime
`pytest.skip()` at collection time, because `--max-skips=0` treats both as violations.

1	# Dev container image for ado-git-repo-insights.
2	#
3	# This image absorbs the per-platform runtime + system-library variance that
4	# native Linux/macOS/Windows setups all encounter (Python 3.12 as the canonical
5	# interpreter, Playwright's Chromium runtime libs, gitleaks, unzip, the GitHub
6	# CLI, GitHub Spec Kit, and the entire.io git-observability CLI).
7	#
8	# **Important — Dev Containers-ready base, not a standalone testable image.**
9	# Per FR-009 (spec 364-devcontainer-refactor), Node.js and pnpm are NOT in this
10	# image. They are provided by the Dev Container Feature
11	# (`ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node`) at devcontainer-up time and the
12	# Corepack activation in `postCreateCommand` (per FR-021). Running
13	# `docker run` against the raw image and expecting `node` / `pnpm` to work is
14	# NOT a supported path — only the Dev Containers lifecycle produces the full
15	# development environment.
16	#
17	# This image does NOT pre-install repo dependencies (`pnpm install`,
18	# `uv sync`, extension Playwright browser download) — those run as
19	# `postCreateCommand` after the workspace is mounted, so the image stays
20	# portable across branches.
21	
22	FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12-bookworm
23	
24	# Pinned versions. Bump deliberately, never via "latest".
25	ARG UV_VERSION=0.11.9
26	ARG GITLEAKS_VERSION=8.18.4
27	# Pinned to match the @playwright/test version in extension/package.json
28	# so `playwright install-deps` resolves the same apt-package list across
29	# image rebuilds. Bump in lockstep when the extension bumps Playwright.
30	ARG PLAYWRIGHT_VERSION=1.60.0
31	# Official SHA256s from `gitleaks_${VERSION}_checksums.txt` published with
32	# the gitleaks GitHub release. Bump alongside GITLEAKS_VERSION; mismatched
33	# downloads fail the build at the `sha256sum -c` step.
34	ARG GITLEAKS_SHA256_AMD64=ba6dbb656933921c775ee5a2d1c13a91046e7952e9d919f9bac4cec61d628e7d
35	ARG REDACTED
36	
37	# GitHub CLI (FR-001). Apt-installed via signed keyring from cli.github.com
38	# with apt-mark hold to prevent future apt-get upgrade drift. The exact
39	# version string must match what cli.github.com publishes for both arches;
40	# D-1b verifies multi-arch availability at PR time.
41	ARG GH_VERSION=2.93.0
42	
43	# GitHub Spec Kit (FR-002). Installed via `uv tool install` from an immutable
44	# git commit pin against github.com/github/spec-kit. Version 0.9.2 is NOT on
45	# public PyPI — only available as the git tag v0.9.2. SPECKIT_COMMIT must
46	# match the dereferenced commit of the tag (D-3a verifies).
47	ARG SPECKIT_VERSION=0.9.2
48	ARG SPECKIT_COMMIT=c3194c543b53c67e85d996fe90bc1b26813b0e3b
49	
50	# entire.io CLI (FR-020). SHA256-verified GitHub release-binary install
51	# (gitleaks-equivalent pattern) — entire.io's install.sh is disqualified by
52	# D-1d for lack of version-pin support. SHA256 values come from
53	# https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/download/v${ENTIRE_VERSION}/checksums.txt
54	ARG ENTIRE_VERSION=0.7.3
55	ARG ENTIRE_SHA256_AMD64=a9a3710855f65726aeec2e5cd55ed3979d883f49a217c5469f1192c9816a9a9d
56	ARG ENTIRE_SHA256_ARM64=e5e6fee7304b220496af8ac2158ad3bb550958fcade75168e75fc0df6295508e
57	
58	# Provided automatically by BuildKit/buildx; falls back to dpkg's own
59	# architecture name when invoked via plain `docker build` (no buildx).
60	# The case statements below map both Docker (amd64/arm64) and uname
61	# (x86_64/aarch64) names to per-tool release-asset suffixes.
62	ARG TARGETARCH
63	
64	# --- Node.js & pnpm: PROVIDED BY DEV CONTAINER LIFECYCLE, NOT THIS IMAGE -----
65	# Node 22 arrives via ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node (digest-pinned in
66	# devcontainer.json). pnpm 9.15.0 arrives via Corepack activation as the FIRST
67	# step of postCreateCommand (per FR-021, fail-closed validation against the
68	# pinned `packageManager` field in root package.json). Do not add Node or
69	# pnpm install steps here — the previous NodeSource + Corepack RUN blocks were
70	# removed per FR-003 + FR-021 (Corepack requires Node, which Features install
71	# at devcontainer-up time, not image-build time).
72	
73	# --- uv -----------------------------------------------------------------------
74	# The base Python image ships pip but not uv. Repo's documented setup path
75	# is uv-driven (uv python install 3.12, uv sync --extra dev), so install
76	# explicitly. `install -m 0755` puts the binary on PATH for all users.
77	RUN curl -LsSf "https://astral.sh/uv/${UV_VERSION}/install.sh" | sh \
78	    && install -m 0755 /root/.local/bin/uv /usr/local/bin/uv \
79	    && install -m 0755 /root/.local/bin/uvx /usr/local/bin/uvx \
80	    && rm -rf /root/.local/bin/uv /root/.local/bin/uvx \
81	    && uv --version
82	
83	# --- GitHub Spec Kit (specify) ------------------------------------------------
84	# FR-002: Install from an immutable git commit pin (NOT PyPI — version 0.9.2
85	# is not published to PyPI). `uv tool install` with explicit UV_TOOL_DIR +
86	# UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR puts the entrypoint at /usr/local/bin so it's accessible to
87	# the vscode user without symlink gymnastics. The Dockerfile's specify pin
88	# (SPECKIT_VERSION + SPECKIT_COMMIT) must match `.specify/init-options.json`
89	# co-committed with this Dockerfile (FR-002 co-commit invariant).
90	#
91	# Version extraction uses the same `grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1`
92	# pattern as the `entire --version` probe below. The previous `awk '{print $NF}'`
93	# idiom worked only because Spec Kit 0.9.2 emits a single-line `specify 0.9.2`
94	# — the entire CLI's multi-line output broke that exact pattern at this
95	# Dockerfile site in PR #416 (CI run 26988692452, fixed in PR #417). Pre-empt
96	# the same regression class for Spec Kit by extracting the first three-part
97	# numeric token from anywhere in the output.
98	RUN UV_TOOL_DIR=/opt/uv-tools UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR=/usr/local/bin \
99	        uv tool install \
100	            "specify-cli @ git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git@${SPECKIT_COMMIT}" \
101	    && installed="$(specify --version 2>&1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1)" \
102	    && [ "$installed" = "${SPECKIT_VERSION}" ] \
103	       || { echo "specify version mismatch: got '$installed', expected '${SPECKIT_VERSION}'" >&2; exit 1; }
104	
105	# --- GitHub CLI (gh) ----------------------------------------------------------
106	# FR-001: Install via cli.github.com apt repository with signed keyring,
107	# pinned version, and apt-mark hold to prevent future apt-get upgrade drift.
108	# Chosen over the Dev Container Feature for stronger determinism + auditability
109	# (E-1 decision, research.md). D-1b confirmed gh ${GH_VERSION} is published
110	# for both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 by the apt repo.
111	RUN install -m 0755 -d /usr/share/keyrings \
112	    && curl -fsSL https://cli.github.com/packages/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
113	        -o /usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
114	    && chmod a+r /usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
115	    && echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg] https://cli.github.com/packages stable main" \
116	        > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/github-cli.list \
117	    && apt-get update \
118	    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gh="${GH_VERSION}*" \
119	    && apt-mark hold gh \
120	    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
121	    && installed="$(gh --version | awk '/^gh version/ {print $3}')" \
122	    && [ "$installed" = "${GH_VERSION}" ] \
123	       || { echo "gh version mismatch: got '$installed', expected '${GH_VERSION}'" >&2; exit 1; }
124	
125	# --- gitleaks ----------------------------------------------------------------
126	# The Debian apt repo's gitleaks lags upstream by 2+ years; install the
127	# official release binary instead so the version is deterministic.
128	# Preflight fails closed if gitleaks is missing — no silent skip.
129	#
130	# Multi-arch: the amd64 (x86_64) and arm64 (aarch64) gitleaks tarballs are
131	# distinct binaries. We must select by build platform — Apple Silicon Mac
132	# / Linux ARM hosts default to a `linux/arm64` base image, where the
133	# `linux_x64` tarball would fail with "Exec format error" at the
134	# `gitleaks version` validation line.
135	#
136	# The download is tee'd to a temp file so we can verify the SHA256 against
137	# the upstream checksums file BEFORE extracting. Defense-in-depth: a
138	# corrupted or substituted release would fail the sha256sum check.
139	RUN set -eux; \
140	    ARCH="${TARGETARCH:-$(dpkg --print-architecture)}"; \
141	    case "$ARCH" in \
142	        amd64|x86_64) GITLEAKS_ARCH="linux_x64"; GITLEAKS_SHA256="$GITLEAKS_SHA256_AMD64" ;; \
143	        arm64|aarch64) GITLEAKS_ARCH="linux_arm64"; GITLEAKS_SHA256="$GITLEAKS_SHA256_ARM64" ;; \
144	        *) echo "Unsupported architecture for gitleaks: $ARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
145	    esac; \
146	    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/gitleaks.tgz \
147	        "https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}/gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_${GITLEAKS_ARCH}.tar.gz"; \
148	    echo "${GITLEAKS_SHA256}  /tmp/gitleaks.tgz" | sha256sum -c -; \
149	    tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin -f /tmp/gitleaks.tgz gitleaks; \
150	    rm /tmp/gitleaks.tgz; \
151	    gitleaks version
152	
153	# --- entire.io CLI ------------------------------------------------------------
154	# FR-020: SHA256-verified GitHub release-binary install (same defense-in-depth
155	# pattern as gitleaks above). entire.io's install.sh is disqualified per D-1d
156	# (no version pinning — script always queries GitHub /releases/latest).
157	#
158	# Multi-arch: amd64 (x86_64) and arm64 (aarch64) entire tarballs are distinct
159	# binaries. SHA256s come from
160	# https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/download/v${ENTIRE_VERSION}/checksums.txt
161	# Bump SHA256 ARGs in lockstep with ENTIRE_VERSION; mismatched downloads fail
162	# the build at the `sha256sum -c` step.
163	RUN set -eux; \
164	    ARCH="${TARGETARCH:-$(dpkg --print-architecture)}"; \
165	    case "$ARCH" in \
166	        amd64|x86_64) ENTIRE_ARCH="amd64"; ENTIRE_SHA256="$ENTIRE_SHA256_AMD64" ;; \
167	        arm64|aarch64) ENTIRE_ARCH="arm64"; ENTIRE_SHA256="$ENTIRE_SHA256_ARM64" ;; \
168	        *) echo "Unsupported architecture for entire: $ARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
169	    esac; \
170	    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/entire.tgz \
